```mermaid
        +set_hinges(hinges)
        +set_property(name, value)
        +calculate_entropy(type, chains, ...)
        +__getitem__(Number)
    }

    Protein "1" --> "1..*" Model : "contains"
    Model "1" --> "1..*" Chain : "contains"
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/protein.py:54-201](), [packman/molecule/model.py:100-408](), [packman/molecule/chain.py:75-333]()

---

## Custom Properties

All three classes support an arbitrary key–value store via `set_property` / `get_property`. This allows user annotations without modifying class definitions.

```python
prot[0]['A'].set_property('disordered', True)
val = prot[0]['A'].get_property('disordered')  # True
```

Properties on `Model` and `Chain` work identically and are stored in a private `__properties` dictionary. They are not persisted when writing to PDB or CIF.

Sources: [packman/molecule/model.py:221-237](), [packman/molecule/model.py:375-392](), [packman/molecule/chain.py:120-136](), [packman/molecule/chain.py:172-188]()

---

## Writing Structures

`Protein.write_structure()` is the recommended output method. It dispatches to `write_pdb` or `write_cif` based on the file extension or the explicit `ftype` argument.

| Format | Method | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| PDB | `write_pdb(filename)` | `.pdb` |
| PDBx/mmCIF | `write_cif(filename)` | `.cif` |
| Auto-detect | `write_structure(filename, ftype)` | either |

The mmCIF format is the default and recommended output format, as it supports structures larger than 99,999 atoms and has richer metadata fields. The PDB format is considered frozen by the wwPDB.

When writing CIF from a PDB-sourced `Protein`, non-coordinate annotations are stored under synthetic `_annotation_index_N` keys. CIF-sourced annotations are written back verbatim.

Sources: [packman/molecule/protein.py:109-200]()

---

## Notes on Model Indexing

- **PDB files:** Model IDs are assigned starting from 0 (using `enumerate`), so `prot[0].get_id()` returns `0`.
- **CIF files:** Model IDs are 1-based, so `prot[0].get_id()` returns `1`.
- In either case, `prot[0]` always accesses the first model by list position.

The `__repr__` of `Model` shows both the ID and the 0-based list index for clarity: e.g., `<Model 1 Index: 0>`.

Sources: [packman/molecule/molecule.py:131](), [packman/molecule/molecule.py:409](), [packman/molecule/model.py:97-98]()

---

# Page: Residue and HetMol

# Residue and HetMol

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [packman/molecule/hetmol.py](packman/molecule/hetmol.py)
- [packman/molecule/protein.py](packman/molecule/protein.py)
- [packman/molecule/residue.py](packman/molecule/residue.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the `Residue` and `HetMol` classes from `packman.molecule`. Both classes sit at the same level in the molecular hierarchy — directly below `Chain` and directly above `Atom` — but they represent different chemical entities. `Residue` models standard amino acid residues (from `ATOM` records in PDB files), while `HetMol` models heterogeneous molecules such as ligands, cofactors, and modified residues (from `HETATM` records).

For the classes above this level (`Protein`, `Model`, `Chain`), see [3.2](#3.2). For the `Atom` and `Bond` classes that sit below, see [3.4](#3.4). For how structures are loaded and these objects are populated, see [3.1](#3.1).

---

## Position in the Hierarchy

**Hierarchy diagram: Molecular object model**

```mermaid
graph TD
    P["Protein"] --> M["Model"]
    M --> C["Chain"]
    C --> R["Residue (ATOM records)"]
    C --> H["HetMol (HETATM records)"]
    R --> A1["Atom"]
    H --> A2["Atom"]
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:35-50](), [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:29-46]()

Both `Residue` and `HetMol` store their child `Atom` objects in an internal dictionary keyed by atom ID, with a parallel name-to-atom lookup dictionary (`__Atoms_Names`). Atoms are assigned to a residue/hetmol at parse time via `__setitem__`.

---

## Residue

Defined in [packman/molecule/residue.py:35-341]().

### Constructor

```python
Residue(id: int, name: str, parent: Chain)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `int` | Residue sequence number as in the PDB file |
| `name` | `str` | Three-letter amino acid code (e.g. `"ALA"`) |
| `parent` | `Chain` | The `Chain` object this residue belongs to |

Internal state initialized at construction:

- `__Atoms`: `None` until first atom is added via `__setitem__`
- `__Atoms_Names`: `{}` — parallel name-to-atom lookup
- `__domain_id`: `None` — populated by hinge prediction
- `__properties`: `{}` — stores computed or user-defined annotations

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:51-61]()

---

### Get Methods

**Diagram: Residue get method map**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Residue"]

    R -->|"get_id()"| id["int: residue sequence number"]
    R -->|"get_name()"| name["str: three-letter code"]
    R -->|"get_parent()"| parent["Chain object"]
    R -->|"get_atoms()"| atoms["generator of Atom (sorted by id)"]
    R -->|"get_atom(key)"| atom["Atom by int id or str name"]
    R -->|"get_calpha()"| ca["Atom where name == 'CA'"]
    R -->|"get_backbone()"| bb["list of Atom: N, CA, C, O"]
    R -->|"get_tip()"| tip["Atom farthest from CA"]
    R -->|"get_centerofgravity()"| cog["numpy.ndarray [x, y, z]"]
    R -->|"get_domain_id()"| did["str or None"]
    R -->|"get_entropy(entropy_type)"| ent["float or None"]
    R -->|"get_property(property_name)"| prop["any stored value"]
    R -->|"get_changed_alphabet()"| alpha["1-letter or 3-letter AA code"]
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:79-185]()

#### Atom Accessors

| Method | Argument | Returns | Notes |
|--------|----------|---------|-------|
| `get_atoms()` | — | `generator` of `Atom` | Sorted by atom ID |
| `get_atom(key)` | `int` or `str` | `Atom` or `None` | Tries ID first, then name |
| `get_calpha()` | — | `Atom` or `None` | Finds atom with `name == 'CA'` |
| `get_backbone()` | — | `list[Atom]` or `None` | Returns atoms named `N`, `CA`, `C`, `O` |
| `get_tip()` | — | `Atom` or `None` | Atom farthest from `CA`; `CA` itself for `GLY` |

`get_calpha()` iterates atoms and returns the first where `name == 'CA'`. [packman/molecule/residue.py:260-270]()

`get_backbone()` is a list comprehension over `get_atoms()` filtering on names `N`, `CA`, `C`, `O`. [packman/molecule/residue.py:292-301]()

`get_tip()` finds the atom with maximum Euclidean distance from `CA` using `Atom.calculate_distance()`. For `GLY`, it returns `CA` directly since glycine has no side chain. If `CA` is absent, `CA` is used as a fallback with a logged warning. [packman/molecule/residue.py:303-328]()

#### Center of Gravity

`get_centerofgravity()` computes a geometric centroid (all atoms given equal mass `= 1`) and returns a `numpy.ndarray` of shape `(3,)`. True atomic masses are not yet applied. [packman/molecule/residue.py:272-290]()

#### Domain ID

`get_domain_id()` returns the domain label set by the hinge prediction algorithm. The domain label format is:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `DM` + number | Rigid domain |
| `FL` + number | Flexible linker (hinge region) |

This field is `None` until hinge prediction has been run. See [4.1](#4.1) for the hinge prediction workflow.

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:129-140]()

#### Entropy Storage

`get_entropy(entropy_type)` reads from the internal `__properties` dict. The only currently recognized `entropy_type` value is `"PackingEntropy"`. If the entropy has not been calculated, a `logging.warning` is emitted. [packman/molecule/residue.py:142-160]()

#### Custom Properties

`get_property(property_name)` and `set_property(property_name, value)` provide a general-purpose key/value store on each residue. Any hashable Python object is a valid key. This can hold user-defined annotations (e.g., disorder flags, experimental labels). [packman/molecule/residue.py:162-177](), [packman/molecule/residue.py:241-257]()

#### Alphabet Conversion

`get_changed_alphabet()` calls `change_alphabet()` from `packman.utilities` on `self.get_name()`, converting between three-letter and one-letter amino acid codes. See [9](#9) for `change_alphabet`. [packman/molecule/residue.py:179-185]()

---

### Set Methods

| Method | Argument | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `set_id(new_id)` | `int` | Overwrite the residue sequence number |
| `set_name(new_name)` | `str` | Overwrite the residue name |
| `set_parent(new_parent)` | `Chain` | Re-assign the parent chain |
| `set_domain_id(new_domain_id)` | `str` | Assign a `DM`/`FL` domain label |
| `set_entropy(entropy_type, value)` | `str`, `float` | Store computed entropy in `__properties` |
| `set_property(property_name, value)` | any, any | Store arbitrary key-value annotation |

`set_entropy()` validates that `entropy_type` is `"PackingEntropy"` before writing. Invalid types emit a `logging.warning` and are not stored. [packman/molecule/residue.py:225-239]()

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:187-257]()

---

### Entropy Calculation Entry Point

```python
Residue.calculate_entropy(
    entropy_type: str,
    chains=None,
    probe_size: float = 1.4,
    onspherepoints: int = 30
)
```

This method does not perform the calculation locally. It delegates upward through the hierarchy: `self.get_parent().get_parent().calculate_entropy(...)`, which resolves to `Model.calculate_entropy()`. Results are then stored back on each residue via `set_entropy()`. For full documentation of the entropy algorithm, see [4.3](#4.3).

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:330-341]()

---

## HetMol

Defined in [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:29-228]().

`HetMol` represents non-standard chemical entities (ligands, water molecules, cofactors, ions) that appear as `HETATM` records in PDB files. Its interface is a subset of `Residue`'s interface, without the amino-acid-specific methods.

### Constructor

```python
HetMol(id: int, name: str, parent: Chain)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `int` | HetMol sequence ID from the PDB file |
| `name` | `str` | Molecule name (e.g. `"HOH"`, `"ATP"`) |
| `parent` | `Chain` | The parent `Chain` object |

Internal state mirrors `Residue`: `__Atoms`, `__Atoms_Names`, `__domain_id`, `__properties`. [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:47-56]()

---

### Get Methods

**Diagram: HetMol get method map**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H["HetMol"]

    H -->|"get_id()"| id["int: sequence ID"]
    H -->|"get_name()"| name["str: molecule name"]
    H -->|"get_parent()"| parent["Chain object"]
    H -->|"get_atoms()"| atoms["generator of Atom (sorted by id)"]
    H -->|"get_atom(key)"| atom["Atom by int id or str name"]
    H -->|"get_centerofgravity()"| cog["numpy.ndarray [x, y, z]"]
    H -->|"get_domain_id()"| did["str or None"]
    H -->|"get_property(property_name)"| prop["any stored value"]
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:77-133]()

`get_atoms()` yields atoms sorted by their ID key. [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:102-108]()

`get_atom(key)` accepts an `int` (atom ID) or `str` (atom name). Tries `__Atoms[key]` first, then `__Atoms_Names[key]`, returns `None` on failure. [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:160-175]()

`get_centerofgravity()` computes an equal-mass centroid and returns a `numpy.ndarray`. Currently uses `i.Coordinates` directly (not `i.get_location()`). [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:209-228]()

`get_domain_id()` and `get_property()` behave identically to the `Residue` equivalents. [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:110-133]()

---

### Set Methods

| Method | Argument | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `set_id(new_id)` | `int` | Overwrite the HetMol ID |
| `set_name(new_name)` | `str` | Overwrite the molecule name |
| `set_parent(new_parent)` | `Chain` | Re-assign the parent chain |
| `set_domain_id(new_domain_id)` | `str` | Assign a `DM`/`FL` domain label |
| `set_property(property_name, value)` | any, any | Store arbitrary key-value annotation |

Sources: [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:135-206]()

---

## Residue vs. HetMol: Feature Comparison

| Feature | `Residue` | `HetMol` |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| `get_id()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_name()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_parent()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_atoms()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_atom(key)` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_centerofgravity()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_domain_id()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_property()` / `set_property()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `set_domain_id()` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `get_calpha()` | ✓ | ✗ |
| `get_backbone()` | ✓ | ✗ |
| `get_tip()` | ✓ | ✗ |
| `get_entropy()` / `set_entropy()` | ✓ | ✗ |
| `calculate_entropy()` | ✓ | ✗ |
| `get_changed_alphabet()` | ✓ | ✗ |

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:79-341](), [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:77-228]()

---

## Class Interaction Diagram

**Diagram: Residue and HetMol relationships to other classes**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Chain["Chain\n(packman.molecule.chain)"]
    Residue["Residue\n(packman.molecule.residue)"]
    HetMol["HetMol\n(packman.molecule.hetmol)"]
    Atom["Atom\n(packman.molecule.atom)"]
    PackingEntropy["PackingEntropy\n(packman.apps)"]
    HingePrediction["predict_hinge()\n(packman.apps)"]
    ChangeAlphabet["change_alphabet()\n(packman.utilities)"]

    Chain -->|"stores Residue objects"| Residue
    Chain -->|"stores HetMol objects"| HetMol
    Residue -->|"get_atoms() / get_atom()"| Atom
    HetMol -->|"get_atoms() / get_atom()"| Atom
    PackingEntropy -->|"set_entropy('PackingEntropy', v)"| Residue
    HingePrediction -->|"set_domain_id('DM...'/'FL...')"| Residue
    HingePrediction -->|"set_domain_id('DM...'/'FL...')"| HetMol
    Residue -->|"get_changed_alphabet()"| ChangeAlphabet
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/residue.py:260-341](), [packman/molecule/hetmol.py:177-188](), [packman/molecule/residue.py:179-185]()

---

## Usage Examples

**Iterating atoms of a residue:**

```python
# mol is a loaded Protein object
for residue in mol[0]['A'].get_residues():
    for atom in residue.get_atoms():
        print(atom.get_name(), atom.get_location())
```

**Accessing specific atoms:**

```python
residue.get_calpha()            # C-alpha atom
residue.get_backbone()          # [N, CA, C, O] atom list
residue.get_atom('CB')          # by name
residue.get_atom(142)           # by atom ID
residue.get_tip()               # atom farthest from CA
```

**Reading domain assignment after hinge prediction:**

```python
domain_label = residue.get_domain_id()   # e.g. 'DM0', 'FL0'
```

**Custom annotations:**

```python
residue.set_property('is_disordered', True)
residue.get_property('is_disordered')    # True
```

**Accessing HetMol atoms (e.g. a ligand):**

```python
for hetmol in mol[0]['A'].get_hetmols():
    print(hetmol.get_name(), hetmol.get_centerofgravity())
    for atom in hetmol.get_atoms():
        print(atom.get_name())
```

---

# Page: Atom, Bond, and Annotations

# Atom, Bond, and Annotations

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [packman/molecule/annotations.py](packman/molecule/annotations.py)
- [packman/molecule/atom.py](packman/molecule/atom.py)
- [packman/molecule/bond.py](packman/molecule/bond.py)

</details>



This page documents the three lowest-level classes in the `packman.molecule` hierarchy: `Atom`, `Bond`, and `Hinge`. These classes represent individual atoms in a structure, covalent and non-covalent connections between atoms, and hinge annotations produced by the hinge prediction algorithm respectively.

For the parent containers that hold `Atom` objects (i.e., `Residue` and `HetMol`), see [3.3](#3.3). For information on how hinge prediction populates `Hinge` objects on a `Chain`, see [4.1](#4.1).

---

## Position in the Molecular Hierarchy

**Diagram: Object Hierarchy with File Locations**

```mermaid
graph TD
    Protein["Protein"] --> Model["Model"]
    Model --> Chain["Chain"]
    Chain --> Residue["Residue"]
    Chain --> HetMol["HetMol"]
    Residue --> Atom["Atom\n[atom.py]"]
    HetMol --> Atom
    Atom -- "get_bonds()" --> Bond["Bond\n[bond.py]"]
    Chain -- "get_hinges()" --> Hinge["Hinge\n[annotations.py]"]
```

`Atom` sits at the bottom of the containment hierarchy. `Bond` connects pairs of `Atom` objects but is not itself part of the containment chain. `Hinge` is a side-channel annotation attached to `Chain`, not embedded in the `Residue`→`Atom` path.

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:34-70](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:25-54](), [packman/molecule/annotations.py:32-52]()

---

## Atom

**Class:** `packman.molecule.Atom`  
**File:** [packman/molecule/atom.py]()

`Atom` is the fundamental data-bearing unit. Every atom parsed from a PDB or CIF file becomes an `Atom` instance, storing the fields defined in the wwPDB record format.

### Constructor

[packman/molecule/atom.py:58-70]()

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | Atom serial number from the structure file |
| `AtomName` | `str` | Atom name (e.g., `CA`, `N`, `OG1`) |
| `Coordinates` | `numpy.ndarray` | 3-element array `[x, y, z]` in Ångströms |
| `Occupancy` | `float` | Occupancy value |
| `bfactor` | `float` | B-factor / temperature factor |
| `Element` | `str` | Chemical element symbol |
| `Charge` | `str` | Formal charge (currently stored as `str`) |
| `parent` | `Residue` or `HetMol` | The containing residue or hetero-molecule |

Two internal stores are also initialized at construction: `__properties` (a dict for user-defined annotations) and `__Bonds` (a list of `Bond` objects).

### Get Methods

**Diagram: Atom Getters and the Data They Return**

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Atom"] -->|"get_id()"| id["int: serial number"]
    A -->|"get_name()"| name["str: atom name"]
    A -->|"get_location()"| loc["numpy.ndarray: [x,y,z]"]
    A -->|"get_occupancy()"| occ["float"]
    A -->|"get_bfactor()"| bf["float"]
    A -->|"get_element()"| el["str"]
    A -->|"get_charge()"| ch["str"]
    A -->|"get_parent()"| par["Residue or HetMol"]
    A -->|"get_domain_id()"| dom["str: DM/FL label"]
    A -->|"get_bonds()"| bonds["List[Bond]"]
    A -->|"get_bond(atom2)"| bond["Bond"]
    A -->|"get_property(name)"| prop["Any"]
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:79-201]()

| Method | Return Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `get_id()` | `int` | Serial number as read from the file |
| `get_name()` | `str` | Atom name string |
| `get_location()` | `numpy.ndarray` | 3D coordinate array |
| `get_occupancy()` | `float` | |
| `get_bfactor()` | `float` | Also used for RMSF in NMR structures |
| `get_element()` | `str` | |
| `get_charge()` | `str` | Will become `float` in a future version |
| `get_parent()` | `Residue` / `HetMol` | Containing residue |
| `get_domain_id()` | `str` | Delegates to `get_parent().get_domain_id()`; returns labels like `DM1` or `FL1` after hinge prediction |
| `get_bonds()` | `List[Bond]` | All bonds involving this atom |
| `get_bond(atom2)` | `Bond` | Specific bond to `atom2` (accepts `Atom` object or integer atom ID) |
| `get_property(name)` | any | Retrieves from the `__properties` dict |

#### `get_bond()` lookup detail

[packman/molecule/atom.py:184-201]()

If `atom2` is passed as an `int`, the method resolves it to an `Atom` by walking up to the `Model` via `get_parent().get_parent().get_parent()` and calling `Model.get_atom(atom2)`. The intersection of both atoms' bond lists is returned.

### Set Methods

| Method | Parameter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `set_id(new_id)` | `int` | |
| `set_name(new_name)` | `str` | |
| `set_parent(new_parent)` | `Residue` / `HetMol` | |
| `set_location(new_location)` | `numpy.ndarray` | |
| `set_occupancy(new_occupancy)` | `float` | |
| `set_bfactor(new_bfactor)` | `float` | |
| `set_elment(new_element)` | `str` | Note: typo in method name (`set_elment`) |
| `set_charge(new_charge)` | `str` | |
| `set_property(name, value)` | any | Stores in `__properties` dict |
| `set_bond(new_bond)` | `Bond` | Appends to `__Bonds` list |

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:203-295]()

> **Note:** The method for setting the element is spelled `set_elment` (missing the 'e') in the current codebase. [packman/molecule/atom.py:252-258]()

### Distance Calculation

```
Atom.calculate_distance(another_atom) -> float
```

[packman/molecule/atom.py:298-307]()

Computes the Euclidean distance in Ångströms between the calling atom and `another_atom` using `numpy.linalg.norm`. This is used extensively by ANM/GNM contact cutoff checks and by packing entropy calculations.

### Custom Properties

Both `get_property` and `set_property` operate on an internal dict `__properties`. This is a general-purpose annotation store: any Python-hashable key can be used to attach arbitrary data to an `Atom` instance. This mechanism is shared across `Atom`, `Bond`, `Residue`, `HetMol`, and `Chain`.

---

## Bond

**Class:** `packman.molecule.Bond`  
**File:** [packman/molecule/bond.py]()

`Bond` represents a connection between exactly two `Atom` objects. It is not part of the containment hierarchy; instead, it is referenced from each of its two atoms via their `__Bonds` list.

### Constructor

[packman/molecule/bond.py:45-54]()

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `int` | Bond serial identifier |
| `atom1` | `Atom` | First atom in the bond |
| `atom2` | `Atom` | Second atom in the bond |
| `type` | `str` | Bond type string (see allowed values below) |
| `source` | `str` or `None` | Origin of the bond information (e.g., `CONNECT` record, algorithm) |

Bonds whose connectivity is not explicitly listed in the structure file are assigned using the rule-based algorithm described in: Zhang et al., *J Cheminform* 4, 26 (2012).

### Allowed Bond Types

[packman/molecule/bond.py:47]()

| Type String | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `non-covalent` | |
| `covalent` | Generic covalent |
| `covalent-single` | Single bond |
| `covalent-double` | Double bond |
| `covalent-triple` | Triple bond |
| `ionic` | |
| `hydrogen` | Hydrogen bond |
| `salt-bridge` | |
| `other` | Catch-all |

`set_type()` validates against this list and logs a warning on invalid input.

### Get Methods

| Method | Return | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `get_id()` | `int` | |
| `get_atoms()` | `(Atom, Atom)` | Returns a tuple `(atom1, atom2)` |
| `get_type()` | `str` | |
| `get_source()` | `str` | |
| `get_property(name)` | any | Custom annotation store |
| `get_torsion(neighbor1, neighbor2, radians=True)` | `float` | Torsion angle in radians or degrees |

Sources: [packman/molecule/bond.py:60-124]()

### Set Methods

| Method | Parameter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `set_atoms(new_pair)` | `(Atom, Atom)` | Validates tuple length == 2 |
| `set_type(new_type)` | `str` | Validated against allowed list |
| `set_property(name, value)` | any | Custom annotation store |
| `set_torsion(theta, neighbor1, neighbor2, radians=True)` | `float` | Rotates the structure |

Sources: [packman/molecule/bond.py:127-198]()

### Torsion Angles

**Diagram: Torsion Angle Four-Atom Requirement**

```mermaid
graph LR
    n1["neighbor1"] --- a1["atom1"]
    a1 --- a2["atom2"]
    a2 --- n2["neighbor2"]
    style a1 stroke-width:2px
    style a2 stroke-width:2px
```

Both `get_torsion` and `set_torsion` require four atoms: the two atoms in the bond (`atom1`, `atom2`) plus one neighbor each. The actual computation is delegated to `Model.get_torsion()` and `Model.set_torsion()` respectively. The `radians` parameter (default `True`) controls units.

[packman/molecule/bond.py:109-124](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:182-198]()

`get_torsion` reads the current dihedral angle; `set_torsion` rotates the atoms to achieve the target angle `theta`.

---

## Hinge Annotation

**Class:** `packman.molecule.Hinge`  
**File:** [packman/molecule/annotations.py]()

`Hinge` is an annotation object produced by the hinge prediction algorithm (`predict_hinge`). It is not part of the `Protein > Model > Chain > Residue > Atom` containment chain, but instances are stored on `Chain` objects and retrieved via `Chain.get_hinges()`. For the algorithm that creates these objects, see [4.1](#4.1).

### Constructor

[packman/molecule/annotations.py:47-52]()

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hid` | `int` | Unique hinge identifier |
| `alpha_value` | `float` | The alpha parameter used when this hinge was detected |
| `elements` | `List[Residue]` | Residue objects that constitute the hinge region |
| `stats` | `List[float]` | Statistical summary of the hinge (e.g., mean/median/mode of B-factors) |
| `p` | `float` | p-value from the permutation test |

### Get Methods

| Method | Return | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `get_id()` | `int` or `None` | |
| `get_alpha_value()` | `float` or `None` | Alpha parameter at which this hinge was detected |
| `get_elements()` | `List[Residue]` | The residues forming this hinge |
| `get_stats()` | list | B-factor statistics for the hinge residues |
| `get_pvalue()` | `float` | p-value from permutation test |

Sources: [packman/molecule/annotations.py:57-96]()

`Hinge` has no set methods; it is constructed once during hinge prediction and treated as read-only.

---

## Relationships Between All Three Classes

**Diagram: Atom, Bond, and Hinge Relationships**

```mermaid
graph TD
    Chain["Chain"] -->|"get_hinges()"| Hinge["Hinge\nannotations.py"]
    Chain -->|"get_residues()"| Residue["Residue"]
    Residue -->|"get_atoms()"| Atom["Atom\natom.py"]
    Atom -->|"get_bonds()"| Bond["Bond\nbond.py"]
    Bond -->|"get_atoms()"| Atom
    Hinge -->|"get_elements()\nreturns List[Residue]"| Residue
    Atom -->|"get_parent()"| Residue
```

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:95-101](), [packman/molecule/atom.py:176-201](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:68-74](), [packman/molecule/annotations.py:74-80]()

---

## Custom Property System

All three classes (`Atom`, `Bond`, and `Hinge` via its element residues) support a general-purpose key-value store via `get_property` / `set_property`. This is consistent across all levels of the hierarchy.

```
atom.set_property('my_score', 0.95)
atom.get_property('my_score')   # returns 0.95

bond.set_property('custom_label', 'active_site')
bond.get_property('custom_label')
```

Any Python dictionary-compatible key can be used. An invalid or missing key logs a warning rather than raising an exception.

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:159-174](), [packman/molecule/atom.py:268-284](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:92-107](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:162-180]()

---

## Summary Reference Table

| Class | File | Key Role | Stored On |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Atom` | `atom.py` | Holds all per-atom data from the structure file | `Residue.__atoms`, `HetMol.__atoms` |
| `Bond` | `bond.py` | Connects two `Atom` objects; carries type and torsion | `Atom.__Bonds` (on both atoms) |
| `Hinge` | `annotations.py` | Annotation produced by hinge prediction; groups residues into hinge regions | `Chain.__hinges` |

Sources: [packman/molecule/atom.py:1-17](), [packman/molecule/bond.py:1-17](), [packman/molecule/annotations.py:1-22]()

# Page: Analysis Applications

# Analysis Applications

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [packman/apps/__init__.py](packman/apps/__init__.py)
- [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py](packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py)
- [packman/apps/dci.py](packman/apps/dci.py)
- [packman/apps/hdanm.py](packman/apps/hdanm.py)
- [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py](packman/apps/predict_hinge.py)
- [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py](packman/bin/PACKMAN.py)
- [packman/bin/__init__.py](packman/bin/__init__.py)
- [packman/entropy/__init__.py](packman/entropy/__init__.py)
- [packman/molecule/__init__.py](packman/molecule/__init__.py)
- [packman/tests/dci/test_dci.py](packman/tests/dci/test_dci.py)

</details>



This page covers the `packman.apps` module: its structure, the four analysis applications it contains, and the shared code pattern used across all of them. For detailed documentation of each individual application, see the child pages: [Hinge Prediction](#4.1), [Dynamic Community Identification (DCI)](#4.2), and [Packing Entropy](#4.3). For the network models that underpin some of these apps, see [Network Models](#5).

---

## Purpose and Scope

`packman.apps` is a collection of bioinformatics analysis pipelines built on top of the `packman.molecule` data model. Each application accepts a `Protein` object (or atoms derived from it) and produces analysis results—either as in-memory objects, written files, or both.

The module does not define new data types; it consumes types defined in `packman.molecule` and `packman.entropy` and delegates geometry work to `packman.geometry` and network models to `packman.anm`.

Sources: [packman/apps/__init__.py:1-18]()

---

## Module Contents

The four applications exported from `packman.apps` are:

| Export | Type | Source File | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `predict_hinge` | function | `predict_hinge.py` | Core hinge prediction logic |
| `hinge_cli` | function | `predict_hinge.py` | CLI wrapper for hinge prediction |
| `DCI` | class | `dci.py` | Dynamic Community Identification |
| `dci_cli` | function | `dci.py` | CLI wrapper for DCI |
| `entropy_cli` | function | `calculate_entropy.py` | CLI wrapper for packing entropy |
| `hdanm_cli` | function | `hdanm.py` | CLI wrapper for hdANM |

Note that `PackingEntropy` (the core entropy class) lives in `packman.entropy`, not in `packman.apps`. The `entropy_cli` function in `packman.apps` is only a thin dispatch wrapper. Similarly, `hdANM` (the core class) lives in `packman.anm`; `hdanm_cli` wraps it.

Sources: [packman/apps/__init__.py:1-18](), [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:1-62](), [packman/apps/hdanm.py:1-64]()

---

## Shared Structural Pattern

Every application follows a two-layer pattern:

**Core layer** — contains the scientific logic. It is callable directly from Python.

**CLI layer** — a `_cli(args, mol)` function that extracts parameters from an `argparse.Namespace` object and calls the core layer. This function is wired into the CLI dispatcher in `packman/bin/PACKMAN.py`.

**Module-level dispatch diagram:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI["packman/bin/PACKMAN.py: load_cli()"] --> A["hinge_cli(args, mol)"]
    CLI --> B["dci_cli(args, mol)"]
    CLI --> C["entropy_cli(args, mol)"]
    CLI --> D["hdanm_cli(args, mol)"]

    A --> E["predict_hinge(atoms, outputfile, Alpha, ...)"]
    B --> F["DCI(mol, cutoff, chain, n_com)"]
    C --> G["PackingEntropy(atoms, chains, probe_size, onspherepoints)"]
    D --> H["hdANM(calpha, dr, power, hng_file)"]

    E --> I["packman.geometry.AlphaShape"]
    F --> J["packman.anm.ANM (GNM Kirchhoff)"]
    G --> K["packman.entropy.PackingEntropy"]
    H --> L["packman.anm.hdANM"]
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:95-131](), [packman/apps/__init__.py:16-18]()

---

## Application Summary

### 1. Hinge Prediction

- **Core:** `predict_hinge(atoms, outputfile, Alpha, method, filename, MinimumHingeLength, nclusters)`
- **CLI wrapper:** `hinge_cli(args, mol)`
- **Input:** A flat list of backbone `Atom` objects from a `Chain`.
- **Method:** Constructs an alpha shape via `AlphaShape`, computes graph eccentricity on the resulting `networkx` graph, clusters eccentricity values with `KMeans`, and identifies contiguous low-eccentricity residue runs as hinges.
- **Output:** Writes a text report to `outputfile`. Attaches `Hinge` objects to the originating `Chain` via `Chain.set_hinges()`. Returns the alpha shape.
- **Key parameter:** `Alpha` — controls the coarseness of the alpha shape. Recommended: `2.8` (closed form), `4.5` (open form).

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:34-65](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:326-366]()

---

### 2. Dynamic Community Identification (DCI)

- **Core:** `DCI` class
- **CLI wrapper:** `dci_cli(args, mol)`
- **Input:** A `Protein` object. Optionally scoped to a single chain.
- **Method:**
  1. Builds a GNM Kirchhoff matrix from Cα coordinates with a distance `cutoff`.
  2. Performs eigendecomposition.
  3. Computes the cross-correlation matrix `C`.
  4. Applies Ward hierarchical clustering on `1 - C`.
  5. Scores cluster counts using the Calinski–Harabasz (CH) criterion to select the optimal number of communities.
- **Output:** Writes PyMOL selection commands to a file via `calcualte_pymol_commands()`. Optionally generates a CH score plot via `calculate_CH_plot()`.
- **Key parameter:** `n_com` — if supplied, skips automatic scoring and uses exactly that many communities.

Sources: [packman/apps/dci.py:28-79](), [packman/apps/dci.py:316-323]()

---

### 3. Packing Entropy

- **Core:** `PackingEntropy` (lives in `packman.entropy`)
- **CLI wrapper:** `entropy_cli(args, mol)` in `packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py`
- **Input:** Atoms from a `Model`, optionally filtered to specific chain IDs.
- **Method:** Voronoi tessellation with configurable probe size and sphere point sampling. Computes per-residue packing fraction and entropy, stored on each `Residue` object.
- **Output (CLI):** Tab-separated table of `Frame`, `Chain`, `ResidueID`, `ResidueName`, `PackingEntropy` written to `args.outputfile`. Also writes total entropy and normalized entropy (`total / (3N-6)`).
- **Key parameters:** `probe_size` (default `1.4` Å, radius of a water molecule), `onspherepoints` (default `30`).

Sources: [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:24-62](), [packman/entropy/__init__.py:1-9]()

---

### 4. hdANM CLI

- **Core:** `hdANM` (lives in `packman.anm`)
- **CLI wrapper:** `hdanm_cli(args, mol)` in `packman/apps/hdanm.py`
- **Input:** Cα atoms from a `Model` or specific chain, plus a `.hng` file specifying domain assignments.
- **Method:** Builds the domain-based Hessian with `hdANM.calculate_hessian(mass_type=...)`, then performs eigendecomposition.
- **Output:** `eigenvalues.csv`, `eigenvectors.csv`, and one PDB movie file per requested mode. Optionally packages all output into a `.tar.gz` archive via `--make_tar`.
- **Key parameters:** `dr` (distance cutoff, default `15` Å), `power` (default `0`), `mass` (`unit` or `residue`).

Sources: [packman/apps/hdanm.py:25-64]()

---

## Dependency Graph

The diagram below maps each application to the modules it depends on.

**App module dependencies:**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    apps["packman.apps"]

    apps --> molecule["packman.molecule"]
    apps --> geometry["packman.geometry"]
    apps --> anm["packman.anm"]
    apps --> entropy_mod["packman.entropy"]

    predict_hinge_fn["predict_hinge()"] --> geometry
    predict_hinge_fn --> molecule

    DCI_cls["DCI"] --> anm
    DCI_cls --> molecule

    entropy_cli_fn["entropy_cli()"] --> entropy_mod
    entropy_cli_fn --> molecule

    hdanm_cli_fn["hdanm_cli()"] --> anm

    apps --> predict_hinge_fn
    apps --> DCI_cls
    apps --> entropy_cli_fn
    apps --> hdanm_cli_fn
```

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:29-32](), [packman/apps/dci.py:25-27](), [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:15-17](), [packman/apps/hdanm.py:23-24]()

---

## CLI Wiring

`packman/bin/PACKMAN.py` defines `load_cli()`, which:

1. Parses the subcommand (`hinge`, `hdanm`, `entropy`, `dci`) via `argparse`.
2. Loads the structure file into a `Protein` object via `molecule.load_structure()`.
3. Dispatches to the appropriate `_cli` function imported from `packman.apps`.

The four `_cli` imports at the top of `PACKMAN.py` are:

```
from ..apps import hinge_cli, hdanm_cli, entropy_cli, dci_cli
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:14-14](), [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:95-131]()

For full CLI argument reference, see [Command-Line Interface](#7). For GUI usage, see [Graphical User Interface (GUI)](#8).

# Page: Hinge Prediction

# Hinge Prediction

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/python-package.yml](.github/workflows/python-package.yml)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py](additional codes/ScanAlpha.py)
- [docs/_static/gallary/logo.ico](docs/_static/gallary/logo.ico)
- [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/compliance.rst](docs/source/tutorials/compliance.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict.rst](docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict.rst)
- [packman/apps/__init__.py](packman/apps/__init__.py)
- [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py](packman/apps/predict_hinge.py)
- [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py](packman/bin/PACKMAN.py)
- [packman/molecule/__init__.py](packman/molecule/__init__.py)
- [packman/molecule/annotations.py](packman/molecule/annotations.py)
- [packman/molecule/atom.py](packman/molecule/atom.py)
- [packman/molecule/bond.py](packman/molecule/bond.py)

</details>



This page documents the hinge prediction application in PACKMAN: the `predict_hinge()` function, its underlying algorithm, the `Hinge` annotation object, the `hinge_cli()` wrapper, and the `ScanAlpha.py` batch utility. For background on how hinge predictions integrate with the broader molecular data model (e.g., how `Hinge` objects are stored on a `Chain`), see the Molecular Data Model page ([3]()) and the Atom/Bond/Annotations page ([3.4]()). For the geometry primitives (`AlphaShape`) that this algorithm depends on, see page [6](). For CLI invocation syntax, see page [7]().

---

## Overview

Hinge prediction in PACKMAN identifies flexible linker regions (hinges) between rigid domains of a protein, using only the static 3D coordinates of backbone atoms. The method models protein packing via **alpha shapes** (a subset of Delaunay tessellations), extracts a graph-theoretic measure (eccentricity) from the resulting contact graph, and clusters eccentricity values to classify residues as hinge or domain.

The key entry point is `predict_hinge()` in [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py]().

**Recommended alpha values:**

| Protein Conformation | Recommended Alpha |
|---|---|
| Closed form | 2.8 |
| Open form | 4.5 |

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:42-43](), [docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict.rst:1-83]()

---

## Algorithm

**Algorithm: Alpha-Shape Hinge Detection**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Backbone Atoms\n(list of packman.molecule.Atom)"] --> B["AlphaShape(atoms, Alpha, get_graph=True)\npackman.geometry"]
    B --> C["alpha_shape\n(tessellation subset)"]
    B --> D["ProteinGraph\n(networkx Graph)"]
    D --> E["eccentricity(ProteinGraph)\nnetworkx"]
    E --> F["centrality_sorted_with_keys\n(per-atom eccentricity array)"]
    F --> G["KMeans(n_clusters=nclusters)\nsklearn"]
    G --> H["central_nodes\n(min eccentricity cluster)"]
    H --> I["HingeResidues\n(residues from central nodes)"]
    I --> J["groupby consecutive IDs"]
    J --> K{"len > MinimumHingeLength?"}
    K -- "Yes" --> L["PredictedHinges list"]
    K -- "No" --> M["Discarded"]
    L --> N["get_statistics()\npermutation_test (mlxtend)"]
    N --> O["Hinge object\npackman.molecule.Hinge"]
    O --> P["Chain.set_hinges(Hinges)"]
    L --> Q["set_domain_id('FLn')\nfor hinge residues"]
    L --> R["set_domain_id('DMn')\nfor domain residues"]
```

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:273-323]()

### Step-by-step description

1. **Alpha shape construction**: `AlphaShape(atoms, Alpha, get_graph=True)` builds the alpha-shape tessellation and a NetworkX graph where nodes are atoms and edges represent adjacency in the shape.
2. **Eccentricity computation**: `networkx.eccentricity(ProteinGraph)` assigns each node (atom) the maximum shortest-path distance to any other node.
3. **K-Means clustering**: Eccentricity values are clustered into `nclusters` groups. The cluster with the lowest centroid value identifies the most "central" (i.e., most constrained, least exposed) atoms — these are the hinge candidates.
4. **Residue grouping**: Atoms in the minimum-eccentricity cluster are mapped to their parent `Residue` objects, sorted by residue ID, and consecutive IDs are grouped using `itertools.groupby`.
5. **Length filtering**: Groups shorter than `MinimumHingeLength` are discarded.
6. **Statistics and p-value**: For each surviving group, B-factors of hinge vs. non-hinge atoms are compared using a permutation test (`mlxtend.evaluate.permutation_test`, 10,000 rounds).
7. **Hinge annotation**: `Hinge` objects are created and attached to the `Chain` via `Chain.set_hinges()`. Hinge residues are labeled `FL0`, `FL1`, … and domain residues are labeled `DM0`, `DM1`, … via `set_domain_id()`.

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:273-323]()

---

## `predict_hinge()` Function

**File**: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:34-324]()

### Signature

```python
predict_hinge(atoms, outputfile, Alpha=float('Inf'), method='alpha_shape',
              filename='Output.pdb', MinimumHingeLength=5, nclusters=4)
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms` | `list[Atom]` | — | Backbone atoms of the protein chain(s) |
| `outputfile` | file | — | Writable file object; receives the text report |
| `Alpha` | `float` | `Inf` | Alpha shape parameter; controls the granularity of the alpha shape |
| `method` | `str` | `'alpha_shape'` | Currently only `'alpha_shape'` is implemented |
| `filename` | `str` | `'Output.pdb'` | Recorded in the output file header for traceability |
| `MinimumHingeLength` | `int` | `5` | Minimum number of consecutive residues to qualify as a hinge |
| `nclusters` | `int` | `4` | Number of KMeans clusters for eccentricity partitioning |

### Return value

Returns `alpha_shape` — the alpha-shape object (subset of Delaunay tessellations) produced by `AlphaShape()`.

### Side effects

- Writes a text report to `outputfile` containing hinge regions, B-factor statistics, p-values, and PyMOL visualization commands.
- Attaches `Hinge` objects to the parent `Chain` via `Chain.set_hinges()`.
- Calls `set_domain_id()` on every residue in the chain (`'FL<n>'` for hinges, `'DM<n>'` for domains).

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:34-65](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:273-323]()

---

## Output: Text Report Format

`predict_hinge()` writes structured text to `outputfile`. The format is:

```
Filename= 1exr.pdb  | Chain(s)= A | AlphaValue= 2.8 | MinimumHingeLength= 5 | EccentricityClusters= 4
Hindge Residues(Predicted):

Hinge #1
Residues: GLY-45 to ALA-60

STATISTICS
        N     Min   Max   Mean  Mode  Median  STDDev
Total   ...
Hinge   ...
NonHinge...

p-value: 0.0023

Pymol Terminal Commands for Visualizing:
color blue, resi 45:60

import plane
plane.make_plane_points(name='HingePlane1', ...)
set cgo_transparency, 0.35, HingePlane1
#--------------------------------------------------#
```

The report includes:
- **Header**: parameters used for the run
- **Per-hinge block**: residue range, B-factor statistics (N, Min, Max, Mean, Mode, Median, StdDev) for total/hinge/non-hinge atoms, p-value, and PyMOL commands
- **Footnotes** (added by `hinge_cli()`): legend for statistics columns and plane visualization instructions

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:92-104](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:297-310](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:336-344]()

---

## `Hinge` Annotation Object

**File**: [packman/molecule/annotations.py:32-96]()

After `predict_hinge()` runs, `Hinge` objects are stored on the `Chain`. Each hinge covers a contiguous sequence of residues.

### Constructor

```python
Hinge(hid, alpha_value, elements, stats, p)
```

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hid` | `int` | Zero-based hinge index within the chain |
| `alpha_value` | `float` | The Alpha parameter used when this hinge was found |
| `elements` | `list[Residue]` | The `Residue` objects comprising this hinge |
| `stats` | `list` | B-factor statistics rows (header + total/hinge/non-hinge) |
| `p` | `float` | p-value from permutation test |

### Accessor methods

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `get_id()` | `int` — hinge index |
| `get_alpha_value()` | `float` — alpha parameter |
| `get_elements()` | `list[Residue]` — residue objects |
| `get_stats()` | nested list — B-factor statistics |
| `get_pvalue()` | `float` — permutation test p-value |

Sources: [packman/molecule/annotations.py:32-96]()

---

## Domain ID Annotation

After hinge prediction, every residue in the chain receives a domain ID string via `set_domain_id()`:

| Domain ID pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FL0`, `FL1`, … | Flexible Linker (hinge) — followed by hinge index |
| `DM0`, `DM1`, … | Domain — followed by domain index |

Domain IDs propagate through the hierarchy: `Atom.get_domain_id()` delegates to `Residue.get_domain_id()`.

**Domain layout diagram (example)**

```mermaid
block-beta
    columns 7
    DM0["DM0\n(Domain 0)"]:2
    FL0["FL0\n(Hinge 0)"]:1
    DM1["DM1\n(Domain 1)"]:2
    FL1["FL1\n(Hinge 1)"]:1
    DM2["DM2\n(Domain 2)"]:1
```

Sources: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:299-321](), [packman/molecule/atom.py:146-157]()

---

## `hinge_cli()` Wrapper

**File**: [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:326-366]()

`hinge_cli()` is the bridge between the argparse CLI layer and `predict_hinge()`. It is called from `packman/bin/PACKMAN.py` when the user runs `python -m packman hinge`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CLI["packman hinge\n(CLI invocation)"] --> PACKMAN["load_cli()\npackman/bin/PACKMAN.py"]
    PACKMAN --> hinge_cli["hinge_cli(args, mol)\npackman/apps/predict_hinge.py"]
    hinge_cli --> backbone_single["get_backbone()\nfor args.chain"]
    hinge_cli --> backbone_all["get_backbone()\nfor each chain in mol[0]"]
    backbone_single --> predict_hinge["predict_hinge(atoms, outputfile, Alpha, ...)"]
    backbone_all --> predict_hinge
    predict_hinge --> WriteOBJ["WriteOBJ(Backbone, alpha_shape, file)\npackman.utilities\n(if --generateobj)"]
```

### Behavior

- If `--chain` is given: processes only that chain and optionally produces a `.obj` file via `WriteOBJ()`.
- If `--chain` is omitted: iterates over all chains in model `0`; chains without backbone atoms are skipped with a warning.
- Appends footnotes to the output file after all chains are processed.
- Flushes both `outputfile` and `logfile` before returning.

### CLI Arguments for `hinge` subcommand

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | positional `float` | — | Alpha shape parameter (2.8 closed, 4.5 open) |
| `filename` | positional `str` | — | Path to PDB/CIF file |
| `--pdbid` | `str` | None | Download PDB from RCSB and save as `filename` |
| `--e_clusters` | `int` | `4` | Number of eccentricity clusters (`nclusters`) |
| `--minhnglen` | `int` | `5` | Minimum hinge length (`MinimumHingeLength`) |
| `--chain` | `str` | None | Specific chain ID; all chains if omitted |
| `--generateobj` | file | None | Write `.obj` file (requires `--chain`) |
| `--outputfile` | file | stdout | Destination for the text report |
| `--logfile` | file | stderr | Destination for log messages |

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:40-48](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:326-366]()

---

## API Usage

### Basic single-chain prediction

```python
from packman import molecule
from packman.apps import predict_hinge

mol = molecule.load_structure('1exr.cif')

# Extract backbone atoms for chain A
backbone = [j for i in mol[0]['A'].get_backbone() for j in i if j is not None]

# Run hinge prediction
predict_hinge(backbone, Alpha=2.8, outputfile=open('output.txt', 'w'))

# Access the resulting Hinge objects
hinges = mol[0]['A'].get_hinges()
for h in hinges:
    print(h.get_id(), h.get_alpha_value(), h.get_pvalue())
    for residue in h.get_elements():
        print(residue.get_id(), residue.get_name())
```

### Scanning multiple alpha values

```python
import numpy
from packman.apps import predict_hinge

for alpha in numpy.arange(0.0, 10.0, 0.5):
    alpha = numpy.around(alpha, decimals=1)
    try:
        predict_hinge(backbone, Alpha=alpha, outputfile=open(f'{alpha}.txt', 'w'))
    except Exception:
        continue

# All Hinge objects from all alpha runs are accumulated on the chain
all_hinges = mol[0]['A'].get_hinges()
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict.rst:35-83]()

## `ScanAlpha.py` Batch Utility

**File**: [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py]()

`ScanAlpha.py` automates the multi-alpha scan and consensus hinge detection workflow. It is not part of the installed package but is provided as a standalone script in the `additional codes/` directory.

```
python3 ScanAlpha.py <filename> [--chain CHAIN] [--begin 0] [--end 10] [--step_size 0.5] [--outfilename output.hng]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `filename` | — | PDB or CIF file path |
| `--chain` | None (all chains) | Chain ID to process |
| `--begin` | `0` | Starting alpha value |
| `--end` | `10` | Ending alpha value |
| `--step_size` | `0.5` | Alpha increment |
| `--outfilename` | `<pdbname>.hng` | Output file path |

### Consensus algorithm

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["For each alpha in [begin, end, step_size]"] --> B["predict_hinge(atoms, Alpha=i, outputfile=trash.txt)"]
    B --> C["Accumulate Hinge objects on Chain"]
    C --> D["Filter: keep only hinges with p-value <= 0.05"]
    D --> E["Pairwise overlap detection\nacross all (alpha, hinge) pairs"]
    E --> F["Union overlapping hinge residue sets"]
    F --> G["Remove hinges touching last 3 residues"]
    G --> H["Sort regions by residue ID"]
    H --> I["Write .hng file\n(D/H records)"]
```

Sources: [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py:30-104]()

### `.hng` File Format

The `.hng` output file is tab-separated. Each line describes one segment:

```
pdbname_A    D1    1:100
pdbname_A    H1    101:120
pdbname_A    D2    121:200
pdbname_A    H2    201:215
pdbname_A    D3    216:Inf
```

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `pdbname_chain` | Base filename (no extension) + `_` + chain ID |
| `D<n>` or `H<n>` | `D` = rigid Domain, `H` = Hinge (flexible linker) |
| `start:end` | Residue ID range (inclusive); `Inf` for the final domain |

This format is consumed by `hdANM` as its `.hng` input file. See page [5.2]() for details.

Sources: [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py:84-103](), [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py:107-143]()

---

# Page: Dynamic Community Identification (DCI)

# Dynamic Community Identification (DCI)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/source/tutorials/dci_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/dci_cli.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst](docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst)
- [packman/apps/__init__.py](packman/apps/__init__.py)
- [packman/apps/dci.py](packman/apps/dci.py)
- [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py](packman/apps/predict_hinge.py)
- [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py](packman/bin/PACKMAN.py)
- [packman/molecule/__init__.py](packman/molecule/__init__.py)
- [packman/tests/dci/test_dci.py](packman/tests/dci/test_dci.py)

</details>



This page documents the `DCI` class and `dci_cli` function in `packman/apps/dci.py`. DCI partitions a protein structure into dynamic communities — groups of residues that move in a correlated manner — using GNM-based cross-correlation and hierarchical clustering. For the underlying GNM theory, see [5.3](#5.3). For CLI argument reference, see [7](#7).

---

## Overview

DCI takes a loaded `Protein` structure, builds a Gaussian Network Model Kirchhoff matrix, computes residue-pair cross-correlations, and clusters the residues using Ward hierarchical clustering. The optimal community count is selected by the Calinski–Harabasz (CH) score, or the user can fix it explicitly.

**Publication:** Kumar, A., Khade, P. M., Dorman, K. S., & Jernigan, R. L. (2022). *Bioinformatics*, 38(10). https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btac159

**Web server:** https://dci.bb.iastate.edu/

---

## Computational Pipeline

**DCI computation flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: packman.molecule.Protein"] --> B["Collect Cα atoms\n(one chain or all chains)"]
    B --> C["calculate_kirchoff()\nBuilds self.GNM_MAT"]
    C --> D["calculate_decomposition()\nStores self.eigen_values,\nself.eigen_vectors"]
    D --> E["calculate_crosscorrelation()\nBuilds self.C via pseudoinverse"]
    E --> F["dist_mat = 1 - self.C"]
    F --> G{n_com provided?}
    G -- "Yes" --> H["get_n_communities(dist_mat, n)\nWard + fcluster(maxclust)"]
    G -- "No" --> I["calculate_cluster(dist_mat)\nIterate k=2..20,\nCalinski-Harabasz score"]
    H --> J["self.store_communities\nself.store_score"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["calcualte_pymol_commands(output_file)\nPyMOL select resi ..."]
    J --> L["calculate_CH_plot()\nSaves pdbid_CH_Score.png"]
```

Sources: [packman/apps/dci.py:43-78]()

---

## The `DCI` Class

**Location:** [packman/apps/dci.py:28-313]()

### Constructor

```python
DCI(mol, cutoff=7.0, chain=None, n_com=None)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mol` | `packman.molecule.Protein` | — | Loaded protein structure |
| `cutoff` | `float` | `7.0` | Distance cutoff (Å) for GNM contact definition |
| `chain` | `str` | `None` | Chain ID to analyse; `None` uses all chains |
| `n_com` | `int` | `None` | Fixed community count; `None` triggers automatic CH-score search |

**Validation:** `n_com` must be ≥ 2 and ≤ number of Cα atoms. `cutoff` must be positive. [packman/apps/dci.py:54-59]()

The constructor runs the full pipeline automatically. After construction, results are accessible through the `get_*` and `calculate_*` methods.

---

### Internal State After Construction

| Attribute | Type | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| `self.atoms` | `list[Atom]` | `__init__` — Cα atoms |
| `self.coords` | `numpy.ndarray` | `__init__` — Cα coordinates |
| `self.GNM_MAT` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_kirchoff` |
| `self.eigen_values` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_decomposition` |
| `self.eigen_vectors` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_decomposition` |
| `self.hessian_inv` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_crosscorrelation` |
| `self.C` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_crosscorrelation` — normalized cross-corr |
| `self.store_communities` | `dict[int, ndarray]` | `calculate_cluster` / `get_n_communities` |
| `self.store_score` | `dict[int, float]` | `calculate_cluster` / `get_n_communities` |
| `self.best_community` | `numpy.ndarray` | `calculate_cluster` (auto mode only) |

---

## Method Reference

**DCI class: methods and their relationships**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DCI {
        +mol: Protein
        +cutoff: float
        +chain: str
        +atoms: list
        +coords: ndarray
        +GNM_MAT: ndarray
        +eigen_values: ndarray
        +eigen_vectors: ndarray
        +hessian_inv: ndarray
        +C: ndarray
        +store_communities: dict
        +store_score: dict
        +best_community: ndarray
        +calculate_kirchoff(gamma)
        +calculate_decomposition()
        +calculate_crosscorrelation()
        +calculate_cluster(dist_mat, max_iter)
        +get_n_communities(dist_mat, n)
        +calculate_CH_plot()
        +calcualte_pymol_commands(output_file)
        +get_cluster_labels()
        +get_crosscorrelation()
        +get_communities()
        +get_labels(community_obj)
        +get_range(iterable)
        +calculate_windows(iterable)
    }
```

Sources: [packman/apps/dci.py:80-313]()

### Calculation Methods

#### `calculate_kirchoff(gamma=1.0)`
[packman/apps/dci.py:159-180]()

Builds the GNM Kirchhoff matrix `self.GNM_MAT` (shape `n × n`). For each pair `(i, j)` of Cα atoms:
- If `distance(i, j) ≤ cutoff`: `GNM_MAT[i,j] = GNM_MAT[j,i] = -gamma`
- Diagonal: `GNM_MAT[i,i] += gamma` per contact

#### `calculate_decomposition()`
[packman/apps/dci.py:182-191]()

Performs symmetric eigendecomposition via `numpy.linalg.eigh(self.GNM_MAT)`. Stores results in `self.eigen_values` and `self.eigen_vectors`.

#### `calculate_crosscorrelation()`
[packman/apps/dci.py:193-207]()

Computes the normalized cross-correlation matrix `self.C`:

1. Pseudoinverse using non-trivial modes (skipping the zero eigenvalue at index 0):  
   `hessian_inv = V[1:].T · diag(1/λ[1:]) · V[1:]`
2. Normalize:  
   `C[i,j] = hessian_inv[i,j] / sqrt(hessian_inv[i,i] · hessian_inv[j,j])`

Values range from −1 (anti-correlated) to +1 (fully correlated).

#### `calculate_cluster(dist_mat, max_iter=21)`
[packman/apps/dci.py:228-255]()

Automatic community detection:
1. Transforms `dist_mat` to Euclidean: `sqrt(2 * dist_mat)`
2. Computes Ward linkage via `scipy.cluster.hierarchy.ward`
3. Iterates community counts from 2 to `max_iter - 1` (default: 2 to 20)
4. Scores each partition with `sklearn.metrics.calinski_harabasz_score`
5. Stores all partitions in `self.store_communities` and scores in `self.store_score`
6. Sets `self.best_community` to the highest-scoring partition

#### `get_n_communities(dist_mat, n)`
[packman/apps/dci.py:117-132]()

User-specified clustering: applies Ward linkage and cuts at exactly `n` clusters via `fcluster(Z, n, criterion='maxclust')`. Sets `self.store_score[n] = 'user-key'`.

### Output Methods

#### `calculate_CH_plot()`
[packman/apps/dci.py:258-275]()

Saves a PNG plot of CH score vs. community count to `{pdbid}_CH_Score.png` in the working directory. Requires `matplotlib`.

#### `calcualte_pymol_commands(output_file)`
[packman/apps/dci.py:277-313]()

Writes a text file with PyMOL-compatible `select resi ...` statements for every community partition stored in `self.store_communities`. Each block is prefixed with community count and CH score. Consecutive residue ranges are compacted (e.g., 10+11+12 → range).

### Accessor Methods

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `get_cluster_labels()` | `self.best_community` — label array for auto-detected best partition |
| `get_crosscorrelation()` | `self.C` — normalized cross-correlation matrix |
| `get_communities()` | `self.store_communities` — dict of all partitions |
| `get_labels(community_obj)` | `dict[label, list[str]]` — residue IDs grouped by cluster label |

---

## CLI Wrapper: `dci_cli`

[packman/apps/dci.py:316-323]()

`dci_cli(args, mol)` is called by the CLI dispatcher in [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:128-129](). It reads `args.chain`, `args.cutoff`, and `args.n_com`, constructs a `DCI` object, and writes PyMOL commands to `args.outputfile`.

**CLI argument table:**

| Argument | Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | positional | `str` | — | Path to PDB or CIF file |
| `--pdbid` | `-pdbid` | `str` | `None` | Download structure by PDB ID before loading |
| `--chain` | `-chain` | `str` | `None` | Single chain to analyse |
| `--cutoff` | `-cutoff` | `float` | `7.0` | GNM distance cutoff in Å |
| `--n_com` | `-n_com` | `int` | `None` | Fixed number of communities |

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:74-79](), [packman/apps/dci.py:316-323]()

**Example CLI invocations:**

```bash
# Auto-detect communities in all chains
python -m packman dci 1prw.pdb

# Fix 5 communities in chain A
python -m packman dci 1prw.pdb --chain A --n_com 5

# Download and analyse
python -m packman dci 1prw.pdb -pdbid 1prw --chain A --cutoff 7.0
```

---

## API Usage

```python
from packman import molecule
from packman.apps import DCI

mol = molecule.load_structure('1prw.cif', ftype='cif')

# Auto community detection (CH score optimization)
dci = DCI(mol, cutoff=7.0, chain='A')

# Best community labels
labels = dci.get_cluster_labels()

# CH score plot
dci.calculate_CH_plot()

# PyMOL commands
with open('communities.txt', 'w') as f:
    dci.calcualte_pymol_commands(f)

# Fixed number of communities
dci2 = DCI(mol, cutoff=7.0, chain='A', n_com=5)
```

Sources: [packman/tests/dci/test_dci.py:1-18](), [packman/apps/dci.py:43-79]()

---

## Distance Metric Detail

The clustering step uses a distance derived from the cross-correlation matrix `self.C`. There are two variants used in the code:

| Mode | Formula applied to `dist_mat = 1 - C` | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| `n_com` (fixed) | `numpy.triu(dist_mat)` | `get_n_communities` |
| Auto (CH search) | `numpy.sqrt(2 * dist_mat)` | `calculate_cluster` |

The `sqrt(2 * (1 - C))` form converts the correlation-based dissimilarity to a proper Euclidean distance (analogous to converting Pearson correlation to Euclidean distance on unit-normalized vectors).

Sources: [packman/apps/dci.py:127-129](), [packman/apps/dci.py:240-243]()

---

## Output Structure

**DCI data and output flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DCI["DCI.__init__()"] --> SC["self.store_communities\ndict: k -> ndarray of labels"]
    DCI --> SS["self.store_score\ndict: k -> float (CH score)"]
    DCI --> BC["self.best_community\nndarray (auto mode only)"]
    SC --> PM["calcualte_pymol_commands()\nWrites text file with\nselect resi ... and chain ..."]
    SS --> CH["calculate_CH_plot()\nSaves pdbid_CH_Score.png"]
    SC --> GL["get_labels(community_obj)\ndict: label -> [residueID+chainID]"]
    GL --> CW["calculate_windows()\nGroups consecutive ranges\nper chain"]
```

Sources: [packman/apps/dci.py:258-313]()

# Page: Packing Entropy

# Packing Entropy

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/source/tutorials/dci_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/dci_cli.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst](docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst)
- [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py](packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py)
- [packman/apps/hdanm.py](packman/apps/hdanm.py)
- [packman/bin/__init__.py](packman/bin/__init__.py)
- [packman/entropy/__init__.py](packman/entropy/__init__.py)
- [packman/entropy/entropy.py](packman/entropy/entropy.py)
- [packman/geometry/__init__.py](packman/geometry/__init__.py)
- [packman/geometry/geometry.py](packman/geometry/geometry.py)
- [packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py](packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py)

</details>



This page documents the `PackingEntropy` class, its underlying Voronoi tessellation algorithm, the `entropy_cli` wrapper, and both API usage patterns. It covers the `packman.entropy` submodule and the `packman.apps.calculate_entropy` module.

For CLI argument reference, see [Command-Line Interface](#7). For the GUI panel, see [Graphical User Interface](#8). For the molecular data model that stores per-residue entropy values, see [Residue and HetMol](#3.3).

---

## Overview

Packing Entropy quantifies how tightly packed each residue is within a protein structure. The metric is derived purely from the 3D geometry of the structure — no simulation or trajectory is required.

The implementation is in [packman/entropy/entropy.py]() and is exposed as `packman.entropy.PackingEntropy`. The CLI wrapper is in [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py]().

> **Citation:** Pranav M. Khade and Robert L. Jernigan. *Entropies Derived from the Packing Geometries within a Single Protein Structure.* ACS Omega 2022 7 (24), 20719-20730. DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.2c00999

---

## Algorithm

The computation proceeds in two phases: surface point generation and Voronoi-based entropy assignment.

**Computation Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: Atom objects + parameters"] --> B["Filter atoms by chain (optional)"]
    B --> C["Build KDTree over atom coordinates"]
    C --> D["calculate_surafacepoints()"]
    D --> D1["For each atom: calculate_spherepoints()"]
    D1 --> D2["Fibonacci sphere around atom\n(onspherepoints samples at radius probe_size + vdw_radius)"]
    D2 --> D3["Discard points with a neighbor closer than sphere_multiplier\n(KDTree.query k=2)"]
    D --> E["surface_points: all retained surface points"]
    E --> F["calculate_entropy()"]
    F --> F1["Concatenate surface_points + atom coordinates"]
    F1 --> F2["scipy.spatial.Voronoi(all_points)"]
    F2 --> F3["For each atom: collect Voronoi cell vertices\ngroup by parent Residue"]
    F3 --> F4["PackingFraction = ConvexHull(atom_coords).volume\n             / ConvexHull(voronoi_vertices).volume"]
    F4 --> F5["PackingEntropy = -R * log10(PackingFraction)"]
    F5 --> G["Residue.set_entropy('PackingEntropy', value)\nResidue.set_property('PackingFraction', value)"]
```

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:101-165]()

### Phase 1 — Surface Point Generation

The method `calculate_spherepoints` generates a point cloud around each atom using a Fibonacci (golden angle) spiral on a sphere. The sphere radius is:

```
sphere_multiplier = (probe_size + vdw_surface_bondi[atom.get_element()]) * 2
```

where `vdw_surface_bondi` is a per-element van der Waals radius lookup from `packman.constants`. Points are retained only if their second-nearest neighbor is farther away than `sphere_multiplier`, which filters out points that fall inside other atoms. The retained points form the approximate solvent-accessible surface.

`calculate_surafacepoints` parallelises this over all atoms using `multiprocessing.dummy.Pool` (thread pool).

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:101-133]()

### Phase 2 — Voronoi Tessellation and Entropy

`calculate_entropy` merges surface points with atom coordinates and passes the combined point cloud to `scipy.spatial.Voronoi`. The surface points act as "phantom" atoms that cap the Voronoi cells of boundary residues, preventing infinite cells.

For each residue:

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| **Packing Fraction** | `ConvexHull(atom_locs).volume / ConvexHull(voronoi_vertices).volume` |
| **Packing Entropy** | `-R × log₁₀(PackingFraction)` |

`R` is the universal gas constant imported from `scipy.constants`. A perfectly packed residue (packing fraction → 1) has entropy → 0. A loosely packed residue (packing fraction → 0) has a large positive entropy.

Both values are stored on the `Residue` object:
- Entropy via `Residue.set_entropy('PackingEntropy', value)`
- Fraction via `Residue.set_property('PackingFraction', value)`

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:135-165]()

---

## Class Reference: `PackingEntropy`

Located at [packman/entropy/entropy.py:31-165]()

### Constructor Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms` | `[Atom]` | required | Atoms to include in the calculation |
| `chains` | `str` / `[str]` / `None` | `None` | Restrict to these chain IDs. `None` includes all chains. |
| `probe_size` | `float` | `1.4` | Radius of the surface probe (Å). Recommended: 1.4 (water molecule radius). |
| `onspherepoints` | `int` | `30` | Number of Fibonacci sphere points generated per atom. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_total_packing_fraction()` | `float` | Sum of `PackingFraction` across all residues |
| `get_total_entropy()` | `float` | Sum of `PackingEntropy` across all residues |
| `get_total_chain_entropy(chain)` | `float` | Sum of `PackingEntropy` for a specific chain |
| `get_surafacepoints()` | `[[float]]` | The computed surface point coordinates |
| `calculate_spherepoints(atom)` | `[[float]]` | Point cloud around a single atom |
| `calculate_surafacepoints()` | `None` | Recomputes and stores `self.surface_points` |
| `calculate_entropy()` | `None` | Runs Voronoi tessellation and stores entropy on residues |

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:68-165]()

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "packman.entropy"
        PE["PackingEntropy\n(entropy.py)"]

        PE --> |"calculate_entropy()"| VT["scipy.spatial.Voronoi"]
        PE --> |"uses"| KD["scipy.spatial.KDTree\n(self.kd_tree)"]
        PE --> |"uses"| CH["scipy.spatial.ConvexHull"]
    end

    end

    end
    subgraph "packman.apps"
        CLI["entropy_cli(args, mol)\n(calculate_entropy.py)"]
    end
    PE --> |"reads"| VDW
    PE --> |"iterates"| AT

    CLI --> |"instantiates"| PE
```

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:1-30](), [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:1-62]()

---

## API Usage

There are two patterns for invoking the calculation.

### Pattern 1 — Via `molecule` Objects

The `Model`, `Chain`, and `Residue` objects each expose a `calculate_entropy` method that delegates to `PackingEntropy` internally. This is the simpler pattern.

```python
from packman import molecule

molecule.download_structure('1LF7')
mol = molecule.load_structure('1LF7.cif')

# Calculate for the full model (all chains)
mol[0].calculate_entropy('PackingEntropy', chains=None, probe_size=1.4, onspherepoints=30)

# Or restrict to specific chains
mol[0]['A'].calculate_entropy('PackingEntropy', chains=None, probe_size=1.4, onspherepoints=30)
```

Retrieve results at any level of the hierarchy:

```python
# Model-level total
mol[0].get_entropy('PackingEntropy')

# Chain-level total
mol[0]['A'].get_entropy('PackingEntropy')

# Per-residue
mol[0].get_residues()[0].get_entropy('PackingEntropy')
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst:19-75]()

### Pattern 2 — Via `PackingEntropy` Directly

This pattern gives access to the full `PackingEntropy` object, including `get_total_packing_fraction`, `get_total_chain_entropy`, and the ability to pass a manually filtered atom list.

```python
from packman import molecule
from packman.entropy import PackingEntropy

molecule.download_structure('1LF7')
mol = molecule.load_structure('1LF7.cif')

result = PackingEntropy(mol[0].get_atoms(), chains='A', probe_size=1.4, onspherepoints=30)

# Access aggregate values
result.get_total_entropy()
result.get_total_packing_fraction()
result.get_total_chain_entropy('A')

# Per-residue values are also stored on Residue objects
for residue in mol[0].get_residues():
    print(residue.get_entropy('PackingEntropy'))
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_api.rst:77-122](), [packman/entropy/entropy.py:42-66]()

### Choosing Between the Two Patterns

| Scenario | Recommended Pattern |
|---|---|
| Standard per-chain or full-model calculation | Pattern 1 (via `molecule` objects) |
| Custom atom filtering (exclude specific residues) | Pattern 2 (via `PackingEntropy` directly) |
| Need access to `get_total_packing_fraction` or `get_surafacepoints` | Pattern 2 |
| Multi-chain exclusion (compute A+B without C) | Pattern 2 with `chains=['A','B']` on full `mol[0].get_atoms()` |

---

## CLI Wrapper: `entropy_cli`

Located at [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:24-62]()

`entropy_cli(args, mol)` is called by the `packman entropy` subcommand. It:

1. Parses `args.chains` as a comma-separated string into a list.
2. Instantiates `PackingEntropy` for each model frame in `mol`.
3. Writes a tab-separated output file with the columns below.
4. Appends a total entropy row and a normalized entropy row (`total / (3N - 6)`).

### Output Format

```
Frame   Chain   ResidueID   ResidueName   PackingEntropy
1       A       10          ALA           0.432
...
Total (Frame 1)                           84.7
Total Normalized Entropy (3N-6) (Frame 1) 0.0023
```

Sources: [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:24-62]()

### CLI Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FILENAME` | required | Path to the PDB/CIF file |
| `-type` | required | Entropy type; only `PackingEntropy` is valid |
| `-pdbid` | `None` | Download PDB by ID and save to `FILENAME` |
| `--chains` | `None` | Comma-separated chain IDs (e.g. `A,B`) |
| `--probe_size` | `1.4` | Surface probe radius in Å |
| `--onspherepoints` | `30` | Fibonacci sphere point count per atom |

Example invocations:

```bash
# Calculate for all chains
packman entropy 1prw.pdb -type PackingEntropy

# Calculate for chains A and B only
packman entropy 1prw.pdb -type PackingEntropy --chains A,B

# Download structure and calculate
packman entropy 1prw.pdb -type PackingEntropy -pdbid 1PRW
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst:23-57]()

---

## Data Flow Summary

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "User/CLI" as user
    participant "entropy_cli / API call" as api
    participant "PackingEntropy.__init__" as init
    participant "calculate_surafacepoints" as surf
    participant "calculate_spherepoints" as sphere
    participant "KDTree" as kdt
    participant "calculate_entropy" as ent
    participant "Voronoi / ConvexHull" as sci
    participant "Residue.set_entropy" as res

    user->>api: atoms, chains, probe_size, onspherepoints
    api->>init: PackingEntropy(atoms, ...)
    init->>kdt: KDTree(coordinates)
    init->>surf: calculate_surafacepoints()
    surf->>sphere: ThreadPool.map(calculate_spherepoints, atoms)
    sphere->>kdt: query(point, k=2)
    sphere-->>surf: retained surface points
    surf-->>init: self.surface_points
    init->>ent: calculate_entropy()
    ent->>sci: Voronoi(surface_points + atom_coords)
    ent->>sci: ConvexHull(atom_locs) and ConvexHull(voronoi_verts)
    ent->>res: set_entropy('PackingEntropy', value)
    ent->>res: set_property('PackingFraction', value)
    res-->>user: retrievable via get_entropy('PackingEntropy')
```

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:42-165](), [packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py:24-62]()

---

## Parameter Guidance

| Parameter | Effect of increasing | Effect of decreasing |
|---|---|---|
| `probe_size` | Larger surface sphere radius; captures more solvent-accessible area | Smaller probe; less surface coverage |
| `onspherepoints` | Denser point cloud per atom; more accurate surface but slower | Faster but coarser surface approximation |

The default `probe_size=1.4` Å corresponds to the van der Waals radius of a water molecule. Values below `1.0` are not recommended per the source documentation. The default `onspherepoints=30` is a balance between accuracy and computation time.

Sources: [packman/entropy/entropy.py:37-41](), [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst:44-50]()

# Page: Network Models

# Network Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [packman/anm/__init__.py](packman/anm/__init__.py)
- [packman/anm/anm.py](packman/anm/anm.py)
- [packman/anm/hd_anm.py](packman/anm/hd_anm.py)
- [packman/gnm/__init__.py](packman/gnm/__init__.py)
- [packman/gnm/gnm.py](packman/gnm/gnm.py)

</details>



This page covers the three elastic network model implementations in PACKMAN: `ANM`, `hdANM`, and `GNM`. It explains their shared mathematical foundation, how they differ architecturally, and when to choose each one.

For detailed API reference for each model, see the child pages:
- Anisotropic Network Model: [ANM](#5.1)
- Hinge-Domain ANM: [hdANM](#5.2)
- Gaussian Network Model: [GNM](#5.3)

The `GNM` class also serves as the backbone of the `DCI` application; for that usage, see [Dynamic Community Identification](#4.2).

---

## Module Layout

The network models live in two subpackages:

| Subpackage | File | Exported Class |
|---|---|---|
| `packman.anm` | `packman/anm/anm.py` | `ANM` |
| `packman.anm` | `packman/anm/hd_anm.py` | `hdANM` |
| `packman.gnm` | `packman/gnm/gnm.py` | `GNM` |

Both subpackages are exposed at the top-level `packman` namespace via their `__init__.py` files ([packman/anm/__init__.py:1-7](), [packman/gnm/__init__.py:1-11]()).

---

## Shared Mathematical Foundation

All three models treat a protein as a network of nodes (atoms or residues) connected by springs. The workflow is identical in structure:

1. **Build a contact/force matrix** from the 3D coordinates and a distance cutoff `dr`.
2. **Decompose** the matrix into eigenvalues and eigenvectors (normal modes).
3. **Derive physical quantities** — fluctuations, cross-correlations, compliance — from the eigenvectors and eigenvalues.

**Contact matrix dimensions:**

| Model | Matrix name | Dimension | Spring weighting |
|---|---|---|---|
| GNM | Kirchhoff | N × N | Scalar (isotropic) |
| ANM | Hessian | 3N × 3N | Tensor (anisotropic) |
| hdANM | Domain Hessian | (6D+3H) × (6D+3H) | Tensor, mass-weighted |

Where N = number of atoms/residues, D = number of rigid domains, H = number of hinge atoms.

**Rigid-body modes:** For a free protein in solution, the six lowest-frequency modes (three translations + three rotations) have zero eigenvalue and are excluded from all physical calculations. All three models skip these in fluctuation and pseudoinverse computations.

**Eigendecomposition methods used:**

| Class | Method called | SciPy/NumPy function |
|---|---|---|
| `GNM` | `calculate_decomposition()` | `numpy.linalg.eigh` |
| `ANM` | `calculate_decomposition()` | `numpy.linalg.eigh` |
| `hdANM` | `calculate_decomposition(include_mass=True)` | `scipy.linalg.eig` (generalized) |

`hdANM` solves a generalized eigenvalue problem `H·v = λ·M·v` with a mass matrix `M`, while `ANM` and `GNM` solve standard symmetric eigenvalue problems ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:216-238](), [packman/anm/anm.py:203-210](), [packman/gnm/gnm.py:153-160]()).

---

**Diagram: Shared Workflow Across All Three Models**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["List[Atom] + parameters"] --> B["Build contact matrix\n(calculate_kirchhoff / calculate_hessian)"]
    B --> C["Eigendecomposition\n(calculate_decomposition)"]
    C --> D["Eigenvalues λ\n(get_eigenvalues)"]
    C --> E["Eigenvectors v\n(get_eigenvectors)"]
    D --> F["Fluctuations / B-factors\n(calculate_fluctuations)"]
    D --> G["Pseudoinverse H⁻¹\n(calculate_hessian_pseudoinverse)"]
    E --> F
    E --> G
    G --> H["Cross-correlation matrix\n(calculate_crosscorrelation / calculate_cross_correlation)"]
```

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:168-229](), [packman/gnm/gnm.py:127-200](), [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:100-508]()

---

## Model Comparison

**Diagram: Class Structure and Key Methods**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GNM {
        +atoms List~Atom~

        +get_crosscorrelation()

    class ANM {
        +atoms List~Atom~
        +gamma float
        +dr float = 15.0
        +power int
        +pf bool
        +hessian ndarray
        +calculate_hessian()
        +calculate_decomposition()
        +calculate_fluctuations()
        +calculate_stiffness_compliance()
```
