```mermaid
        +get_hessian()
        +get_eigenvalues()
        +get_eigenvectors()
        +get_fluctuations()
        +get_stiffness_map()
        +get_compliance_map()
    }
    class hdANM {
        +atoms List~Atom~
        +hng_file str
        +gamma float
        +dr float = 15.0
        +power int
        +pf bool
        +domain_hessian ndarray
        +domain_mass_matrix ndarray
        +RT_eigen_vectors ndarray
        +calculate_hessian(mass_type)
        +calculate_decomposition(include_mass)
        +calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()
        +calculate_fluctuations()
        +calculate_cross_correlation(n_modes)
        +calculate_movie(mode_number, extrapolation)
        +get_hessian()
        +get_eigenvalues()
        +get_eigenvectors()
        +get_RT_eigen_vectors()
        +get_fluctuations()
        +get_crosscorrelation_matrix()
    }
```

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:32-201](), [packman/anm/anm.py:38-312](), [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:60-509]()

---

### Key Differences

| Feature | GNM | ANM | hdANM |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix type | Kirchhoff (scalar contacts) | Hessian (directional forces) | Domain-compressed Hessian |
| Default cutoff `dr` | 7.3 Å | 15.0 Å | 15.0 Å |
| Dimensionality | N × N | 3N × 3N | (6D+3H) × (6D+3H) |
| Mass weighting | No | No | Yes (`unit`/`atom`/`residue`) |
| Requires `.hng` file | No | No | Yes |
| Fluctuations | Scalar per residue | Vector magnitude per atom | Via RT eigenvectors |
| Movie generation | No | Linear only | Linear and curvilinear |
| Stiffness/compliance | No | Yes | No |
| Cross-correlation | Yes | Indirectly via H⁻¹ | Yes |

---

## Constructor Parameters

All three constructors accept `atoms` as a `List[Atom]` (from `packman.molecule`). The remaining parameters control the spring model:

| Parameter | Type | ANM default | hdANM default | GNM default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gamma` | float | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 | Spring constant |
| `dr` | float | 15.0 | 15.0 | 7.3 | Distance cutoff (Å) |
| `power` | int | 0 | 0 | 0 | Exponent for distance weighting |
| `pf` | bool | False | False | — | Parameter-free mode |
| `hng_file` | str | — | required | — | Path to `.hng` hinge/domain file |

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:52-68](), [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:79-97](), [packman/gnm/gnm.py:45-54]()

---

## hdANM: Domain-Compressed Representation

`hdANM` is a structural extension of `ANM`. Instead of tracking 3 degrees of freedom per atom, it tracks:
- **6 degrees of freedom per rigid domain** (3 translational + 3 rotational)
- **3 degrees of freedom per hinge atom** (same as ANM)

The resulting compressed Hessian has this block structure:

```
H_new = | HDD  HDH |
        | HHD  HHH |
```

Where HDD (domain-domain), HHD/HDH (hinge-domain coupling), and HHH (hinge-hinge) blocks are assembled from standard ANM Hessian blocks via `get_hessian_block()` ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:176-212]()).

The domain/hinge membership for each atom is read from the `.hng` file using `load_hinge()` from `packman.utilities`, then stored on each residue via `set_domain_id()` ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:263-268]()).

After decomposition, `calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()` "explodes" the compressed (6D+3H)-dimensional eigenvectors back to full 3N-dimensional displacement vectors, which are then used for fluctuations and movie generation ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:411-444]()).

**Diagram: hdANM Data Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    HNG[".hng file\n(load_hinge)"] --> DOMAIN["Domain/hinge\nassignment per atom\n(set_domain_id)"]
    ATOMS["List[Atom]\n(Ca atoms)"] --> DOMAIN
    DOMAIN --> BLOCKS["ANM Hessian blocks\n(get_hessian_block)"]
    BLOCKS --> COMPRESSED["Domain Hessian\n(6D+3H) x (6D+3H)\n(domain_hessian)"]
    ATOMS --> MASS["Mass matrix M\n(domain_mass_matrix)\nmass_type: unit/atom/residue"]
    COMPRESSED --> GENEIG["Generalized eigenproblem\nscipy.linalg.eig(H, M)\n(calculate_decomposition)"]
    MASS --> GENEIG
    GENEIG --> EVec["Eigenvectors\n(eigen_vectors)"]
    GENEIG --> EVal["Eigenvalues\n(eigen_values)"]
    EVec --> RT["RT eigenvectors\n3N x modes\n(calculate_RT_eigen_vectors)"]
    RT --> FLUCT["Fluctuations\n(calculate_fluctuations)"]
    RT --> MOVIE["Movie frames\n(calculate_movie)"]
    RT --> XCORR["Cross-correlation\n(calculate_cross_correlation)"]
```

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:241-509]()

---

## When to Use Each Model

| Use case | Recommended model |
|---|---|
| Fast per-residue flexibility / B-factor prediction | `GNM` |
| Residue-residue cross-correlations for community detection (`DCI`) | `GNM` |
| Directional mode shapes and animations | `ANM` |
| Stiffness and compliance analysis | `ANM` |
| Proteins with known hinge regions and rigid domains | `hdANM` |
| Mass-weighted normal modes for hinge motion | `hdANM` |
| Curvilinear (physically realistic) domain motion animation | `hdANM` |

---

## Typical Usage Pattern

All three models follow the same imperative "calculate then get" pattern:

```
# Step 1: construct with atoms and parameters
model = ANM(atoms, gamma=1.0, dr=15.0)

# Step 2: build matrix
model.calculate_hessian()          # or calculate_kirchhoff() for GNM

# Step 3: decompose
model.calculate_decomposition()

# Step 4: derive quantities
model.calculate_fluctuations()

# Step 5: retrieve results
fluct = model.get_fluctuations()
evals = model.get_eigenvalues()
evecs = model.get_eigenvectors()
```

For `hdANM`, an extra step is needed after decomposition to recover full-resolution vectors:

```
model.calculate_hessian(mass_type='residue')
model.calculate_decomposition(include_mass=True)
model.calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()
model.calculate_fluctuations()
```

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:168-229](), [packman/gnm/gnm.py:127-186](), [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:216-471]()

---

# Page: Anisotropic Network Model (ANM)

# Anisotropic Network Model (ANM)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py](packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py)
- [packman/tests/data/4hla.hng](packman/tests/data/4hla.hng)
- [packman/tests/entropy/test_entropy.py](packman/tests/entropy/test_entropy.py)

- [packman/tests/utilities/test_utilities.py](packman/tests/utilities/test_utilities.py)

</details>



This page covers the `ANM` class in `packman/anm/anm.py`: its constructor parameters, the sequence of calculation steps (Hessian → decomposition → fluctuations / stiffness-compliance / movie), and the get/calculate API pattern. For the hinge-domain extension that wraps and restructures the ANM Hessian into domain/hinge blocks, see [hdANM](#5.2). For the scalar (isotropic) counterpart, see [GNM](#5.3).

---

## Overview

The `ANM` class implements the Anisotropic Network Model, a coarse-grained elastic network model in which residues (represented by Cα atoms or any `Atom` objects) are connected by harmonic springs within a distance cutoff. The resulting Hessian matrix is diagonalized to yield normal modes, which are used to derive:

- Theoretical B-factors (fluctuations)
- Stiffness and compliance maps and per-residue profiles
- Multi-frame structural movies of individual modes

The class follows a consistent two-step API: every `calculate_*` method populates an internal attribute, and the corresponding `get_*` method returns it.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:1-35](), [packman/anm/__init__.py:1-7]()

---

## Module Location

```
packman/
└── anm/
    ├── __init__.py     # exports ANM and hdANM
    └── anm.py          # ANM class definition
```

The `packman.anm` subpackage exports two classes:

| Symbol | File | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `ANM` | `packman/anm/anm.py` | Standard anisotropic network model |
| `hdANM` | `packman/anm/hd_anm.py` | Hinge-domain ANM (extends ANM concepts) |

Sources: [packman/anm/__init__.py:1-7]()

---

## Constructor

```
ANM(atoms, gamma=1.0, dr=15.0, power=0, pf=False)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `atoms` | `List[Atom]` | required | Ordered list of `packman.molecule.Atom` objects |
| `gamma` | `float` | `1.0` | Uniform spring constant (must be > 0) |
| `dr` | `float` | `15.0` | Distance cutoff in Å (must be > 0) |
| `power` | `int` | `0` | Exponent added to distance in spring weighting; used only in parameter-free mode |
| `pf` | `bool` | `False` | Enables parameter-free mode; requires `power > 0` |

On construction the class stores atom coordinates as a `numpy.ndarray` (`self.coords`) and initializes all result attributes (`hessian`, `fluctuations`, `stiffness_map`, etc.) to `None`.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:52-74]()

---

## Calculation Workflow

**Typical ANM (fluctuations) workflow diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["ANM(atoms, gamma, dr, power, pf)"] --> B["calculate_hessian()"]
  B --> C["calculate_decomposition()"]
  C --> D["calculate_fluctuations()"]
  C --> E["calculate_stiffness_compliance()"]
  C --> F["calculate_movie(mode_number)"]
  D --> G["get_fluctuations()"]
  E --> H["get_stiffness_map()"]
  E --> I["get_compliance_map()"]
  E --> J["get_stiffness_profile()"]
  E --> K["get_compliance_profile()"]
  F --> L["writes mode_number.cif or .pdb"]
```

All `calculate_*` methods return `True` on success. Results are stored in instance attributes and retrieved via the corresponding `get_*` methods.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:167-311]()

---

## Hessian Matrix

**Method:** `calculate_hessian()` → populates `self.hessian`

**Retrieve with:** `get_hessian()` → `numpy.ndarray` of shape `(3N, 3N)`

The Hessian is a `3N × 3N` symmetric matrix (N = number of atoms). Each off-diagonal `3×3` block `H_ij` for atoms `i` and `j` within the cutoff is:

```
H_ij = −γ / |r_ij|^(2+power)  ×  (r_j − r_i)⊗(r_j − r_i)
```

The diagonal block `H_ii` is the negative sum of all off-diagonal blocks in that row (ensures translational invariance). Pairs outside the cutoff (`|r_ij| > dr`) contribute zero.

When `pf=True`, the matrix is further element-wise divided by a distance matrix (parameter-free weighting), enabling distance-dependent spring constants.

**Hessian construction diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  coords["self.coords (3D array of N atoms)"] --> loop["Loop over all i,j pairs"]
  loop --> dist_check{"dist <= dr?"}
  dist_check -- "Yes" --> outer["outer product rij⊗rij scaled by -gamma/dist^(2+power)"]
  dist_check -- "No" --> zero["H_ij = 0"]
  outer --> off["hessian[i*3:i*3+3, j*3:j*3+3]"]
  outer --> diag["hessian[i*3:i*3+3, i*3:i*3+3] -= block"]
  off --> pf_check{"pf is not None?"}
  pf_check -- "Yes" --> pf_divide["element-wise divide by distance_mat"]
  pf_check -- "No" --> done["self.hessian"]
  pf_divide --> done
```

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:168-201]()

---

## Eigendecomposition

**Method:** `calculate_decomposition()` → populates `self.eigen_values`, `self.eigen_vectors`

**Retrieve with:** `get_eigenvalues()`, `get_eigenvectors()` → `numpy.ndarray`

Uses `numpy.linalg.eigh` (real symmetric eigensolver) on the Hessian:

```python
self.eigen_values, self.eigen_vectors = numpy.linalg.eigh(self.hessian)
```

The result is sorted ascending. For a system of N atoms, there are `3N` eigenvalues. The **first 6 are near-zero** (rigid-body translational and rotational modes) and are excluded from all downstream analyses.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:203-210]()

---

## Fluctuations (Theoretical B-factors)

**Method:** `calculate_fluctuations(endmode=None)` → populates `self.fluctuations`

**Retrieve with:** `get_fluctuations()` → list of N floats

For each non-rigid mode `k` (modes 6 through 3N−1), the contribution to residue `i`'s mean-square displacement is:

```
Δᵢₖ = (uₓ² + u_y² + u_z²)_ik / λ_k
```

The total fluctuation for residue `i` is the sum over all non-rigid modes. These are the theoretical B-factors analogous to crystallographic B-factors.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:212-229]()

---

## Stiffness and Compliance Analysis

**Method:** `calculate_stiffness_compliance()` → populates four attributes

**Retrieve with:**

| Method | Returns | Shape |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `get_stiffness_map()` | `numpy.ndarray` | `N × N` |
| `get_compliance_map()` | `numpy.ndarray` | `N × N` |
| `get_stiffness_profile()` | list of floats | `N` |
| `get_compliance_profile()` | list of floats | `N` |

**Algorithm:**

1. Compute the pseudoinverse of the Hessian using the non-rigid eigenvectors and eigenvalues:
   ```
   H⁺ = EVec[6:].T × diag(1/λ[6:]) × EVec[6:]
   ```
2. For each ordered pair `(i, j)`, construct a unit force vector `F_ij` directed from atom `i` to atom `j`.
3. Solve for the displacement vector `d = H⁺ · F_flat`.
4. Compliance = projection of the differential displacement onto the force direction.
5. Stiffness = 1 / compliance.

Per-residue profiles are the row-wise `nanmean` of the respective maps.

> **Citation:** Scaramozzino et al., *Structural Compliance – A New Metric for Protein Flexibility*, Proteins, 2020. DOI: 10.1002/prot.25968

**Stiffness/compliance data flow diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  ev["eigen_vectors, eigen_values (from calculate_decomposition)"] --> pinv["H_inv = EVec6plus.T @ diag(1/lambda6plus) @ EVec6plus"]
  pinv --> loop2["For each pair i,j"]
  loop2 --> Fvec["Build force vector FMAT[i]=-Fij, FMAT[j]=+Fij"]
  Fvec --> displacement["d = H_inv @ FMAT_flat"]
  displacement --> comp["compliance = dot(d_diff, Fij)"]
  comp --> stiff["stiffness = 1 / compliance"]
  stiff --> maps["stiffness_map[i][j], compliance_map[i][j]"]
  maps --> profiles["stiffness_profile = nanmean(rows), compliance_profile = nanmean(rows)"]
```

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:232-274](), [docs/source/tutorials/compliance.rst:1-118]()

---

## Movie Generation

**Method:** `calculate_movie(mode_number, scale=1.5, n=20, ftype='cif')` → writes a multi-model structure file

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode_number` | `int` | required | Index into eigenvector array (first non-rigid = 6) |
| `scale` | `float` | `1.5` | Amplitude multiplier |
| `n` | `int` | `20` | Number of frames (ideally a multiple of 4, minimum 8) |
| `ftype` | `str` | `'cif'` | Output format: `'cif'` or `'pdb'` |

The method generates `n+1` frames by advancing a sine-wave phase over a full period. For each frame `j`:

```
x_new = x0 + scale × sin(j/n × 2π) × eigenvector[mode_number]
```

Each frame is a `Model` object containing displaced `Atom` instances. All frames are assembled into a `Protein` object and written to `{mode_number}.{ftype}`.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:276-311]()

---

## Usage Example

The following pattern comes from the compliance tutorial and the test suite:

```python
from packman import molecule
from packman.anm import ANM

# Load structure
mol = molecule.load_structure('1LF7.cif')

# Select C-alpha atoms from model 0
c_alpha = [i for i in mol[0].get_calpha() if i is not None]

# Build model
anm_model = ANM(c_alpha, gamma=1.0, dr=15.0)

# Step 1: build Hessian
anm_model.calculate_hessian()

# Step 2: decompose
anm_model.calculate_decomposition()

# Step 3a: compute fluctuations
anm_model.calculate_fluctuations()
fluctuations = anm_model.get_fluctuations()

# Step 3b: compute stiffness/compliance
anm_model.calculate_stiffness_compliance()
stiffness_map     = anm_model.get_stiffness_map()
compliance_map    = anm_model.get_compliance_map()
stiffness_profile = anm_model.get_stiffness_profile()

# Step 3c: generate movie for mode 6 (first non-rigid mode)
anm_model.calculate_movie(6, scale=1.5, n=20, ftype='cif')
# writes: 6.cif
```

For parameter-free mode (distance-dependent spring constants):

```python
anm_pf = ANM(c_alpha, pf=True, dr=float('inf'), power=3)
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/compliance.rst:37-75](), [packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py:41-60]()

---

## Parameter Notes

| Parameter | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| `gamma` | Uniform spring constant. Larger values stiffen all springs equally; does not affect relative mode shapes, only eigenvalue magnitudes. |
| `dr` | Distance cutoff in Å. Increasing this value adds longer-range interactions; `float('inf')` creates a fully connected network. |
| `power` | Used only when `pf=True`. Exponent applied to inter-atom distance in the denominator, making close atoms stiffer. Typical values: 2–3. |
| `pf` | When `True`, applies distance-dependent weighting; requires `power > 0`. |

**Validation on construction:** If `pf=True` and `power <= 0`, the constructor raises `Exception`. If `gamma <= 0` or `dr <= 0`, the constructor raises `Exception`.

Sources: [packman/anm/anm.py:52-67]()

---

## Tests

The test suite for `ANM` is in [packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py:41-63](). The `test_ANM_Compliance` test:

1. Loads `packman/tests/data/4hla.cif`
2. Extracts all Cα atoms from model 0
3. Runs the full pipeline: `calculate_hessian` → `calculate_decomposition` → `calculate_stiffness_compliance` → `calculate_fluctuations`
4. Validates eigenvalues against a pre-computed reference array using `numpy.allclose`
5. Asserts all four outputs (`stiffness_map`, `compliance_map`, `stiffness_profile`, `compliance_profile`) are non-None

Sources: [packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py:41-63]()

This page documents the `hdANM` class in `packman/anm/hd_anm.py`, its domain-based Hessian construction, mass matrix assembly, eigendecomposition, RT eigenvector transformation, and the `hdanm_cli` wrapper. For the standard all-atom ANM without domain partitioning, see [ANM (5.1)](#5.1). For hinge prediction that produces the required `.hng` input, see [Hinge Prediction (4.1)](#4.1).

---

## Overview

hdANM (Hinge-Domain ANM) is an extension of ANM that explicitly accounts for rigid-domain structure. Protein regions are partitioned into **domains** (rigid bodies, 6 DOF each) and **hinges** (flexible atoms, 3 DOF each). This reduces the Hessian dimensionality from `3N × 3N` to `(6D + 3H) × (6D + 3H)`, where D = number of domains and H = number of hinge atoms. The result is a model that captures large-scale domain motions constrained by hinge flexibility.

**Citation:** Khade et al., *Biophysical Journal*, 2021. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bpj.2021.10.017

---

## The .hng File Format

The `.hng` (hinge) file is the required input that defines how residues are classified as domains or hinges. It is tab-delimited, one segment per line.

**Columns:**

| Column | Content | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `Filename_ChainID` | `1exr.pdb_A` |
| 2 | Segment ID (prefix `D` = domain, `H` = hinge) | `D1`, `H1`, `D2` |
| 3 | Residue range `start:end` (inclusive) | `1:70` |

**Example** (from `packman/tests/data/1prw.hng`):

```
1exr.pdb_A    D1    1:70
1exr.pdb_A    H1    71:90
1exr.pdb_A    D2    91:149
```

This defines two domains (`D1`, `D2`) separated by one hinge (`H1`). The hinge file can be generated by the PACKMAN hinge prediction algorithm or written manually.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:11-24](), [packman/tests/data/1prw.hng:1-3](), [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst:47-55]()

---

## Class Constructor

The `hdANM` class is located in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:60-95]() and exported from `packman/anm/__init__.py`.

```
hdANM(atoms, hng_file, gamma=1.0, dr=15.0, power=0, pf=False)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `atoms` | `List[Atom]` | required | Atom objects (typically C-alpha atoms) |
| `hng_file` | `str` | required | Path to the `.hng` file |
| `gamma` | `float` | `1.0` | Spring constant |
| `dr` | `float` | `15.0` | Distance cutoff in Å |
| `power` | `float` | `0` | Distance power (for non-parametric mode) |
| `pf` | `bool` | `False` | Parameter-free mode flag |

The constructor loads the `.hng` file via `load_hinge(hng_file)` from `packman.utilities`, storing the domain/hinge range map as `self.HNGinfo`. Atom coordinates are stored as a numpy array in `self.coords`.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:79-95](), [packman/anm/__init__.py:1-7]()

---

## Computation Workflow

**Workflow Diagram: hdANM Step Sequence**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["hdANM(atoms, hng_file)"] --> B["calculate_hessian(mass_type)"]
    B --> C["calculate_decomposition(include_mass)"]
    C --> D["calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()"]
    D --> E1["calculate_fluctuations()"]
    D --> E2["calculate_movie(mode_number)"]
    D --> E3["calculate_hessian_pseudoinverse(n_modes)"]
    E3 --> E4["calculate_cross_correlation(n_modes)"]

    B -.->|"stores"| F1["domain_hessian\ndomain_mass_matrix\ndomain_info"]
    C -.->|"stores"| F2["eigen_values\neigen_vectors"]
    D -.->|"stores"| F3["RT_eigen_vectors"]
    E1 -.->|"stores"| F4["fluctuations"]
    E3 -.->|"stores"| F5["hessian_pseudoinverse"]
    E4 -.->|"stores"| F6["crosscorrelation_matrix"]
```

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:216-509]()

---

## Hessian Construction

`calculate_hessian(mass_type='unit')` builds the reduced-dimension Hessian and mass matrix. It is implemented in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:241-408]().

### Step 1: Assign Domain IDs

Each atom's parent residue is assigned a domain ID (`D1`, `H1`, etc.) by matching its residue number against the `HNGinfo` ranges. This calls `residue.set_domain_id()`.

### Step 2: Build Sub-matrices

The domain Hessian has a block structure assembled from four sub-matrices. `get_hessian_block(i, j)` computes the standard ANM 3×3 interaction block between atom indices `i` and `j` ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:176-211]()).

**Block Structure Diagram: Domain Hessian H_new**

```mermaid
block-beta
  columns 2
  HDD["HDD\n6D × 6D\n(Domain–Domain)"] HDH["HDH\n6D × 3H\n(Domain–Hinge)"]
  HHD["HHD\n3H × 6D\n(Hinge–Domain)"] HHH["HHH\n3H × 3H\n(Hinge–Hinge)"]
```

| Block | Dimensions | Construction |
|-------|-----------|--------------|
| `HDD` | `6D × 6D` | Domain-domain interactions; each atom pair contributes a 3×3 block extended with cross-product terms for torque components |
| `HDH` | `6D × 3H` | Domain-hinge interactions; transpose of `HHD` |
| `HHD` | `3H × 6D` | Hinge-domain interactions; 3×3 block extended with rotational terms |
| `HHH` | `3H × 3H` | Hinge-hinge interactions; direct sum of 3×3 ANM blocks |

Each domain has **6 degrees of freedom**: 3 translational (`F_Delta`) and 3 rotational (`Torque_Phi`). The center of mass (COM) of each domain is computed as the arithmetic mean of its atom coordinates ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:297]()).

### Step 3: Assemble H_new

`H_new` is assembled as:

```
H_new[0:6D, 0:6D]   = HDD
H_new[0:6D, 6D:]    = HDH
H_new[6D:,  0:6D]   = HHD
H_new[6D:,  6D:]    = HHH
```

[packman/anm/hd_anm.py:344-350]()

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:241-408]()

---

## Mass Matrix

`calculate_hessian()` also builds the mass matrix `M` with the same block structure. Three mass assignment modes are supported via the `mass_type` parameter:

| `mass_type` | Hinge atom mass | Domain translational mass | Domain rotational mass |
|-------------|----------------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| `'unit'` | Identity (1 per DOF) | `len(atoms_in_domain)` × I₃ | Sum of unit inertia tensors |
| `'atom'` | `atomic_weight[element]` | Sum of atomic weights | Weighted inertia tensors |
| `'residue'` | `amino_acid_molecular_weight[residue_name]` | Sum of residue molecular weights | Weighted inertia tensors |

The rotational block `M[3:,3:]` for each domain is the **inertia tensor** computed from atom positions relative to the domain COM. Constants are sourced from `packman.constants.atomic_weight` and `packman.constants.amino_acid_molecular_weight`.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:352-408]()

---

## Eigendecomposition

`calculate_decomposition(include_mass=True)` is implemented in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:216-238]().

- **With mass** (`include_mass=True`): Uses `scipy.linalg.eig(domain_hessian, domain_mass_matrix)` — a **generalized eigenvalue problem**. Eigenvalues are sorted by ascending real part.
- **Without mass** (`include_mass=False`): Uses `numpy.linalg.eigh(domain_hessian)` — standard symmetric eigendecomposition.

The resulting `eigen_values` and `eigen_vectors` are stored on the instance. The first 6 eigenvalues correspond to rigid-body modes and are excluded from physical analysis.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:216-238]()

---

## RT (Reverse Transformed) Eigenvectors

`calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()` is implemented in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:411-443]().

The hdANM eigenvectors have dimension `(6D+3H) × (6D+3H)`. For visualization and fluctuation analysis, they must be mapped back to `3N × (6D+3H)` space (one 3-vector per atom). This expansion is called the **Reverse Transform** (previously called "exploded vectors" before version 1.3.3).

**Transformation Rules:**

- **Domain atom** (prefix `D`): The domain's 6-vector `[Δx, Δy, Δz, φx, φy, φz]` is converted to a per-atom 3-vector using the rotation-translation formula:
  - `new_x = Δx + φy·(z - COM_z) - φz·(y - COM_y)`
  - `new_y = Δy + φz·(x - COM_x) - φx·(z - COM_z)` *(sign conventions per code)*
  - `new_z = Δz + φx·(y - COM_y) - φy·(x - COM_x)`
- **Hinge atom** (prefix `H`): The atom's 3-vector is taken directly from the eigenvector's hinge section.

Result is stored in `self.RT_eigen_vectors` as a `(3N) × (6D+3H)` matrix.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:411-443]()

---

## Fluctuations (Theoretical B-factors)

`calculate_fluctuations()` is implemented in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:446-471]().

Uses RT eigenvectors. For each non-rigid mode `k` (starting at index 6):

```
fluctuation[atom_i] = Σ_k  (rx_k² + ry_k² + rz_k²) / λ_k
```

where `rx_k`, `ry_k`, `rz_k` are the RT eigenvector components for atom `i` in mode `k`, and `λ_k` is the corresponding eigenvalue.

Result stored in `self.fluctuations` as a list of length `N`.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:446-471]()

---

## Hessian Pseudoinverse and Cross-Correlation Matrix

### Pseudoinverse

`calculate_hessian_pseudoinverse(n_modes='all')` ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:473-489]()) computes:

```
H⁺ = V[6:n]ᵀ · diag(1/λ[6:n]) · V[6:n]
```

where `V` is the `RT_eigen_vectors` matrix transposed (rows = modes). Rigid modes (indices 0–5) are excluded. The result is stored as `self.hessian_pseudoinverse` with shape `(3N, 3N)`.

The `get_hessian_pseudoinverse(n_modes)` getter will auto-compute if not already present.

### Cross-Correlation Matrix

`calculate_cross_correlation(n_modes='all')` ([packman/anm/hd_anm.py:491-508]()) computes the normalized dynamic cross-correlation:

```
C[i,j] = Tr(H⁺[i,j]) / sqrt( Tr(H⁺[i,i]) · Tr(H⁺[j,j]) )
```

Result stored as `self.crosscorrelation_matrix` with shape `(N, N)`.

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:473-508]()

---

## Movie Generation

`calculate_movie(mode_number, scale=1.5, n=20, extrapolation='curvilinear', ftype='cif', ca_to_aa=False)` is implemented in [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:510-]().

Generates a multi-model structure file representing the oscillatory motion of a given mode.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode_number` | `int` | required | Index into `eigen_vectors`; mode 6 is first non-rigid |
| `scale` | `float` | `1.5` | Amplitude multiplier |
| `n` | `int` | `20` | Number of frames; should be ≥ 8 and ideally a multiple of 4 |
| `extrapolation` | `str` | `'curvilinear'` | `'linear'` or `'curvilinear'` |
| `ftype` | `str` | `'cif'` | Output file format: `'cif'` or `'pdb'` |
| `ca_to_aa` | `bool` | `False` | Propagate Cα motion to all atoms of the residue |

**Frame positions** use a sinusoidal sweep: `sin(k · 2π/n)` for frame `k`.

**Extrapolation methods:**

- `'linear'`: Each atom displaced linearly along its eigenvector direction. Domain atoms use the translation + small-angle rotation approximation.
- `'curvilinear'`: Domain atoms use the Rodrigues rotation formula for physically correct large-angle rigid-body rotation. This avoids structural distortions at larger amplitudes.

Output is written as `{mode_number}.cif` or `{mode_number}.pdb` in the working directory, as a multi-model `Protein` object using `prot.write_structure()`.

**Movie Generation Flow:**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["calculate_movie(mode_number)"] --> B["sinusoidal movement array\nn frames"]
    B --> C{"extrapolation type"}
    C -->|"linear"| D["translation + small-angle\nrotation per domain atom"]
    C -->|"curvilinear"| E["Rodrigues rotation formula\nper domain atom"]
    D --> F["Atom objects in AtomsOfTheFrame"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["Model objects in ModelsOfTheProtein"]
    G --> H["Protein.write_structure()\nmode_number.cif/.pdb"]
```

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:510-]()

---

| Method | Returns | Prerequisite calls |
|--------|---------|-------------------|
| `get_hessian()` | `domain_hessian` (ndarray) | `calculate_hessian()` |
| `get_eigenvalues()` | `eigen_values` (ndarray) | `calculate_hessian()`, `calculate_decomposition()` |
| `get_eigenvectors()` | `eigen_vectors` (ndarray) | `calculate_hessian()`, `calculate_decomposition()` |
| `get_RT_eigen_vectors()` | `RT_eigen_vectors` (ndarray, 3N × modes) | `calculate_decomposition()`, `calculate_RT_eigen_vectors()` |
| `get_fluctuations()` | `fluctuations` (list, length N) | `calculate_fluctuations()` |
| `get_hessian_pseudoinverse(n_modes)` | `hessian_pseudoinverse` (ndarray, 3N × 3N) | auto-computes if absent |
| `get_crosscorrelation_matrix(n_modes)` | `crosscorrelation_matrix` (ndarray, N × N) | auto-computes if absent |

Sources: [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:99-174]()

## hdanm_cli Wrapper

`hdanm_cli(args, mol)` in `packman/apps/hdanm.py` is the CLI entry point for hdANM analysis.

**Execution flow:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["hdanm_cli(args, mol)"] --> B["Extract calpha atoms\nfrom mol[0] or mol[0][chain]"]
    B --> C["hdANM(calpha, dr, power, hng_file)"]
    C --> D["calculate_hessian(mass_type=args.mass)"]
    D --> E["calculate_decomposition()"]
    E --> F["generate_output()"]
    F --> G1["numpy.savetxt eigenvalues.csv"]
    F --> G2["numpy.savetxt eigenvectors.csv"]
    F --> G3["calculate_movie(i) for i in 6..6+modes"]
    H{"args.make_tar?"} -->|"yes"| I["write to tempdir\npack into tar.gz"]
    H -->|"no"| J["write to working directory"]
    F --> H
```

**CLI Arguments** (from `packman hdanm`):

Output files written: `eigenvalues.csv`, `eigenvectors.csv`, and one structure file per mode (e.g., `6.cif`, `7.cif`, …).

## API Usage Example

The following sequence replicates the steps shown in [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst:20-132]():

1. Load structure and extract Cα atoms:
   - `molecule.load_structure('1exr.cif')` → `mol`
   - `calpha = [i for i in mol[0]['A'].get_calpha() if i is not None]`

2. Instantiate:
   - `Model = hdANM(calpha, dr=15, power=0, hng_file='1exr.pdb.hng')`

3. Build Hessian with residue masses:
   - `Model.calculate_hessian(mass_type='residue')`

4. Decompose:
   - `Model.calculate_decomposition()`

5. Generate movie for mode 6 (first non-rigid):
   - `Model.calculate_movie(6, scale=2, n=10)` → writes `6.cif`

6. Get cross-correlation using first 10 non-rigid modes:
   - `Model.get_crosscorrelation_matrix(n_modes=10)` → `(N × N)` ndarray

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst:20-132](), [packman/anm/hd_anm.py:60-508]()

# Page: Gaussian Network Model (GNM)

# Gaussian Network Model (GNM)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/_static/gallary/bond_rotate.png](docs/_static/gallary/bond_rotate.png)
- [docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst](docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/alpha_shape.rst](docs/source/tutorials/alpha_shape.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/bond_rotate.rst](docs/source/tutorials/bond_rotate.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/molecule.rst](docs/source/tutorials/molecule.rst)
- [packman/gnm/__init__.py](packman/gnm/__init__.py)
- [packman/gnm/gnm.py](packman/gnm/gnm.py)
- [packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py](packman/tests/anm/test_anm.py)
- [packman/tests/data/4hla.hng](packman/tests/data/4hla.hng)
- [packman/tests/entropy/test_entropy.py](packman/tests/entropy/test_entropy.py)
- [packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py](packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py)
- [packman/tests/molecule/test_molecule.py](packman/tests/molecule/test_molecule.py)
- [packman/tests/utilities/__init__.py](packman/tests/utilities/__init__.py)
- [packman/tests/utilities/test_utilities.py](packman/tests/utilities/test_utilities.py)

</details>



This page documents the `GNM` class in the `packman.gnm` subpackage: its constructor parameters, the Kirchhoff matrix construction, eigendecomposition, fluctuation calculation, pseudoinverse, and cross-correlation matrix. This page covers the GNM as a standalone model. For usage of GNM results inside the Dynamic Community Identification workflow, see [DCI](#4.2). For the anisotropic counterpart (ANM and hdANM), see [ANM](#5.1) and [hdANM](#5.2).

---

## Overview

The Gaussian Network Model represents a protein as a network of residues connected by Hookean springs. Residues whose Cα atoms are within a cutoff distance `dr` are connected. The topology is encoded in an N×N **Kirchhoff matrix** (Γ). Eigendecomposition of Γ gives normal modes whose inverse eigenvalues weight residue mobility. GNM is isotropic: it models only the *magnitude* of fluctuations, not their direction.

**Module location**: `packman/gnm/gnm.py`, exposed via `packman/gnm/__init__.py`.

```python
from packman.gnm import GNM
```

Sources: [packman/gnm/__init__.py:1-11](), [packman/gnm/gnm.py:1-30]()

---

## Class: `GNM`

### Constructor

```python
GNM(atoms, gamma=1.0, dr=7.3, power=0)
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `atoms` | `List[Atom]` | required | Cα atoms (or any point set) to model |
| `gamma` | `float` | `1.0` | Uniform spring constant |
| `dr` | `float` | `7.3` | Distance cutoff in Å (see Yang et al. 2009) |
| `power` | `int` | `0` | Distance power exponent (non-parametric mode) |

Validation: both `gamma` and `dr` must be positive; an `Exception` is raised otherwise.

3D coordinates are extracted immediately from `atoms` via `get_location()` and stored as a NumPy array in `self.coords`.

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:45-58]()

---

## Computation Workflow

The `GNM` class follows a sequential calculate-then-get pattern. All results start as `None` and are populated by their respective `calculate_*` methods.

**Computation flow diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["GNM(atoms, gamma, dr, power)"] --> B["calculate_kirchhoff()"]
    B --> C["calculate_decomposition()"]
    C --> D["calculate_fluctuations(endmode)"]
    C --> E["calculate_crosscorrelation()"]
    D --> F["get_fluctuations()"]
    D --> G["get_pseudoinverse()"]
    E --> H["get_crosscorrelation()"]
    E --> G
    B --> I["get_kirchhoff()"]
    C --> J["get_eigenvalues()"]
    C --> K["get_eigenvectors()"]
```

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:60-200](), [packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py:15-35]()

---

## Kirchhoff Matrix

**Method**: `calculate_kirchhoff(gamma=1.0) → bool`

Builds the N×N Kirchhoff (Laplacian) matrix Γ. For each pair of residues (i, j):

- If Euclidean distance ≤ `dr`:
  - `Γ[i, j] = Γ[j, i] = −γ`
  - `Γ[i, i] += γ`  
  - `Γ[j, j] += γ`

The diagonal entry for residue i equals the number of contacts it makes (its coordination number), scaled by γ. The resulting matrix is symmetric, positive semi-definite, and singular (it has exactly one zero eigenvalue corresponding to rigid-body translation).

Retrieved via `get_kirchhoff() → numpy.ndarray` (shape N×N).

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:128-151]()

---

## Eigendecomposition

**Method**: `calculate_decomposition() → bool`

Decomposes the Kirchhoff matrix using `numpy.linalg.eigh` (symmetric eigensolver):

```
Γ = U Λ Uᵀ
```

- Eigenvalues stored in `self.eigen_values` (ascending order; λ₀ ≈ 0)
- Eigenvectors stored in `self.eigen_vectors` (columns are eigenvectors)

Retrieved via:
- `get_eigenvalues() → numpy.ndarray`
- `get_eigenvectors() → numpy.ndarray`

The first eigenvalue is effectively zero (numerical precision ~10⁻¹⁵). All subsequent eigenvalues λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ … ≤ λₙ₋₁ are positive.

**Expected eigenvalue spectrum** (example from test data `4hla.cif`, chain A, 99 Cα atoms):

| Mode index | Eigenvalue |
|-----------|-----------|
| 0 | ~1.13 × 10⁻¹⁵ (zero) |
| 1 | 0.2494 |
| 2 | 0.2841 |
| 3 | 0.4324 |
| … | … |
| 98 | 15.54 |

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:153-160](), [packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py:16-27]()

---

## Fluctuations (Theoretical B-factors)

**Method**: `calculate_fluctuations(endmode=None) → bool`

Computes the pseudoinverse of Γ by summing spectral contributions from modes 1 through `stop_at` (skipping mode 0):

```
Γ⁺ = Σᵢ₌₁ᴺ⁻¹  (1/λᵢ) · uᵢ uᵢᵀ
```

The diagonal of Γ⁺ gives the mean-square fluctuation of each residue, proportional to its theoretical B-factor:

```
⟨Δrᵢ²⟩ = (3 k_B T / γ) · Γ⁺[i, i]
```

The `endmode` parameter limits the sum to the first `endmode` modes, allowing mode-subset analysis.

| Result | Accessor |
|--------|----------|
| Pseudoinverse matrix (N×N) | `get_pseudoinverse()` |
| Per-residue fluctuations (length N) | `get_fluctuations()` |

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:162-186]()

---

## Cross-Correlation Matrix

**Method**: `calculate_crosscorrelation() → bool`

Recomputes the pseudoinverse via matrix multiplication (slightly different numerical path from `calculate_fluctuations`), then normalizes to produce the N×N cross-correlation matrix:

```
C[i, j] = Γ⁺[i, j] / sqrt(Γ⁺[i, i] · Γ⁺[j, j])
```

Values range from −1 to +1:
- `+1`: perfectly correlated motion (same direction)
- `0`: uncorrelated
- `−1`: perfectly anti-correlated motion (opposite directions)

The pseudoinverse here is computed as:

```
Γ⁺ = U₁:ₙ · diag(1/λ₁, …, 1/λₙ₋₁) · U₁:ₙᵀ
```

where `U₁:ₙ` are the non-trivial eigenvectors (rows 1..N−1 of `EVec = eigen_vectors.T`).

Retrieved via `get_crosscorrelation() → numpy.ndarray` (shape N×N).

> **Note**: Both `calculate_fluctuations` and `calculate_crosscorrelation` write to `self.pseduinverse`. The last one called wins. Call `get_pseudoinverse()` only after the method whose pseudoinverse you want.

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:188-200]()

---

## API Reference Summary

**Methods and their relationships to stored state:**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GNM {
        +atoms List

        +gamma float
        +dr float
        +power int
        +kirchhoff ndarray
        +eigen_values ndarray
        +eigen_vectors ndarray
        +fluctuations ndarray
        +pseduinverse ndarray
        +crosscorrelation ndarray
        +calculate_kirchhoff(gamma) bool
        +calculate_decomposition() bool
        +calculate_fluctuations(endmode) bool
        +calculate_crosscorrelation() bool
        +get_kirchhoff() ndarray
        +get_eigenvalues() ndarray

        +get_crosscorrelation() ndarray
    }
```

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:32-200]()

---

## Complete Usage Example

```python
from packman import molecule
from packman.gnm import GNM

# Step 1: Load structure and extract Cα atoms
mol = molecule.load_structure('1prw.cif')
calpha = [i for i in mol[0]['A'].get_calpha() if i is not None]

# Step 2: Construct the model
model = GNM(calpha, gamma=1.0, dr=7.3, power=0)

# Step 3: Build Kirchhoff matrix
model.calculate_kirchhoff()
kirchhoff = model.get_kirchhoff()  # shape (N, N)

# Step 4: Eigendecomposition
model.calculate_decomposition()
eigenvalues  = model.get_eigenvalues()   # shape (N,)
eigenvectors = model.get_eigenvectors()  # shape (N, N)

# Step 5a: Fluctuations (theoretical B-factors)
model.calculate_fluctuations()
fluctuations = model.get_fluctuations()  # shape (N,)
pseudoinv    = model.get_pseudoinverse() # shape (N, N)

# Step 5b: Cross-correlation matrix (also recomputes pseudoinverse)
model.calculate_crosscorrelation()
crosscorr = model.get_crosscorrelation() # shape (N, N)
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst:1-97](), [packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py:9-38]()

---

## Parameter Notes

| Parameter | Recommended value | Reference |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|
| `dr` | 7.3 Å | Yang et al., *PNAS* 106, 2009 |
| `gamma` | 1.0 (relative units) | Tirion, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 77, 1996 |
| `power` | 0 (standard GNM) | — |

The default cutoff `dr=7.3` is the value established by Yang et al. (2009) as the range that maximizes cooperativity in elastic network models. Using a smaller cutoff captures fewer contacts and produces sparser matrices; a larger cutoff captures more contacts and can reduce mode resolution for flexible regions.

Sources: [packman/gnm/gnm.py:42-43](), [docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst:10-13]()

---

## Testing

The test suite in `packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py` validates:

1. `calculate_kirchhoff()` returns `True`
2. `calculate_decomposition()` returns `True`
3. Eigenvalues match expected numerical values within tolerance `rtol=1e-7, atol=1e-7` (99-element spectrum for chain A of `4hla.cif`)
4. `calculate_crosscorrelation()` and `calculate_fluctuations()` execute without error
5. `get_crosscorrelation()`, `get_fluctuations`, and `get_pseudoinverse` all return non-`None`

Test data used: `packman/tests/data/4hla.cif`, chain A, 99 Cα atoms, `gamma=1`, `dr=7.3`, `power=1`.

Sources: [packman/tests/gnm/test_gnm.py:1-38]()

# Page: Geometry Module

# Geometry Module

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/_static/gallary/bond_rotate.png](docs/_static/gallary/bond_rotate.png)
- [docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst](docs/source/tutorials/GNM.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/alpha_shape.rst](docs/source/tutorials/alpha_shape.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/bond_rotate.rst](docs/source/tutorials/bond_rotate.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/molecule.rst](docs/source/tutorials/molecule.rst)
- [packman/entropy/entropy.py](packman/entropy/entropy.py)
- [packman/geometry/__init__.py](packman/geometry/__init__.py)
- [packman/geometry/geometry.py](packman/geometry/geometry.py)
- [packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py](packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py)

</details>



The `packman.geometry` module provides low-level geometric primitives used internally by higher-level analyses in PACKMAN. It contains two public functions: `AlphaShape` and `Circumsphere`. These functions operate directly on `packman.molecule.Atom` objects and form the computational backbone of hinge prediction (see [Hinge Prediction](#4.1)). The Packing Entropy module (see [Packing Entropy](#4.3)) uses Voronoi tessellations from `scipy` independently and does not call into `packman.geometry`.

---

## Module Layout

**Diagram: packman.geometry module structure**

```mermaid
graph TD
    pkg["packman.geometry"]
    init["packman/geometry/__init__.py"]
    impl["packman/geometry/geometry.py"]
    pkg --> init
    init -->|"exports Circumsphere"| impl
    init -->|"exports AlphaShape"| impl
    impl -->|"scipy.spatial.Delaunay"| scipy["scipy"]
    impl -->|"networkx.Graph"| nx["networkx"]
    impl -->|"Atom.get_location()"| atom["packman.molecule.Atom"]
```

Sources: [packman/geometry/__init__.py:1-10](), [packman/geometry/geometry.py:1-30]()

---

## Public API

Both functions are exported at the `packman.geometry` level.

```python
from packman.geometry import AlphaShape, Circumsphere
```

| Function | Signature | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `Circumsphere` | `(Tetrahedron: List[Atom]) -> (Centre, Radius)` | NumPy array of 3D center, float radius |
| `AlphaShape` | `(atoms, alpha, get_graph=True)` | Tessellations list, optionally also a `networkx.Graph` |

Sources: [packman/geometry/__init__.py:9-10](), [packman/geometry/geometry.py:31-115]()

---

## `Circumsphere`

[packman/geometry/geometry.py:31-57]()

Given exactly **four** points (a tetrahedron), `Circumsphere` computes the unique sphere that passes through all four points.

**Input:** A list of four `packman.molecule.Atom` objects, or four `[X, Y, Z]` coordinate lists. Coordinates are retrieved via `Atom.get_location()`.

**Output:** A tuple `(Centre, Radius)` where:
- `Centre` — a NumPy array `[x, y, z]` of the sphere center.
- `Radius` — a Python `float` giving the circumradius.

**Method:** Uses determinant-based linear algebra. Five matrices (`alpha_mat`, `gamma_mat`, `Dx_mat`, `Dy_mat`, `Dz_mat`) are assembled from atom coordinates, and `numpy.linalg.det` is applied to each. The center components are `Dx/(2*alpha)`, `Dy/(2*alpha)`, `Dz/(2*alpha)` and the radius is `sqrt(Dx² + Dy² + Dz² − 4·alpha·gamma) / (2·|alpha|)`.

**Diagram: Circumsphere data flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["List of 4 Atom objects"]
    B["Atom.get_location()"]
    C["alpha_mat, gamma_mat,\nDx_mat, Dy_mat, Dz_mat"]
    D["numpy.linalg.det()"]
    E["Centre array, Radius float"]
    A --> B --> C --> D --> E
```

Sources: [packman/geometry/geometry.py:31-57]()

---

## `AlphaShape`

[packman/geometry/geometry.py:60-115]()

Computes the **alpha shape** of a set of atoms: a subset of the full Delaunay tessellation retaining only those tetrahedra whose circumsphere radius is less than the cutoff `alpha`.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms` | Iterable of `Atom` | — | Atoms to tessellate |
| `alpha` | `float` | — | Radius cutoff (Å). Use `float('Inf')` for the full Delaunay tessellation |
| `get_graph` | `bool` | `True` | Whether to return the `networkx.Graph` in addition to tessellations |

### Return Values

- **`AlphaShape` (list):** Each element is a list of four `Atom` objects forming one accepted tetrahedron.
- **`ProteinGraph` (`networkx.Graph`):** Nodes are atom indices (integer positions in `atoms`); edges connect every pair of atoms that share an accepted tetrahedron. Only returned when `get_graph=True`.

### Internal helper: `calculate_alphafitness`

[packman/geometry/geometry.py:80-96]()

A nested function that applies the alpha test: returns `True` if `circumradius < alpha`, `False` otherwise.

### Algorithm

**Diagram: AlphaShape computation pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["atoms: List[Atom]"]
    B["Delaunay([i.get_location() for i in atoms])\nDelaunayTessellations"]
    C["Iterate DelaunayTessellations.simplices\n(each simplex = 4 atom indices: a,b,c,d)"]
    D["Circumsphere([atoms[a],atoms[b],atoms[c],atoms[d]])\n-> Centre, Radius"]
    E["calculate_alphafitness(alpha, Radius)\nRadius < alpha?"]
    F["Accept tetrahedron\nAppend to AlphaShape\nAdd nodes/edges to ProteinGraph"]
    G["Discard tetrahedron"]
    H["Return AlphaShape, ProteinGraph"]
    A --> B --> C --> D --> E
    E -->|"True"| F --> H
    E -->|"False"| G
```

Sources: [packman/geometry/geometry.py:98-115]()

### Alpha parameter semantics

| `alpha` value | Effect |
|---|---|
| Small (e.g. 2–4 Å) | Only tight, densely packed clusters retained |
| Large | More tetrahedra retained |
| `float('Inf')` | All Delaunay tetrahedra retained; equivalent to full Delaunay tessellation |

> **Tip from the source:** If you need tessellations at multiple alpha cutoffs, compute once with `alpha=float('Inf')` to get all simplices, then filter by circumradius yourself using `Circumsphere`. This avoids repeated Delaunay computation.

Sources: [packman/geometry/geometry.py:63-70]()

---

## Usage in PACKMAN

**Diagram: Where geometry functions are consumed**

```mermaid
graph LR
    G1["geometry.AlphaShape"]
    G2["geometry.Circumsphere"]
    H["packman.apps\nhinge prediction\n(predict_hinge)"]
    E["packman.entropy\nPackingEntropy\n(uses scipy.spatial.Voronoi,\nnot packman.geometry)"]
    G1 -->|"backbone atoms, alpha param"| H
    G2 -->|"called internally by AlphaShape"| G1
    H -.->|"not used"| E
```

- **Hinge prediction** (`packman.apps`) calls `AlphaShape` with backbone atoms and a user-supplied `alpha` value. The resulting `ProteinGraph` is used to identify disconnected regions at given alpha values, which correspond to hinge locations. See [Hinge Prediction](#4.1) for full details.
- **Packing Entropy** (`packman.entropy.PackingEntropy`) does **not** use `packman.geometry`. It uses `scipy.spatial.Voronoi` and `scipy.spatial.ConvexHull` directly. See [Packing Entropy](#4.3).

Sources: [packman/geometry/geometry.py:60-115](), [packman/entropy/entropy.py:19-20](), [packman/entropy/entropy.py:135-164]()

---

## API Usage Example

The following illustrates the typical API pattern documented in the alpha shape tutorial:

```
# Step 1: load structure
from packman.molecule import load_structure, download_structure
from packman.geometry import AlphaShape, Circumsphere

download_structure('1exr')
mol = load_structure('1exr.cif')

# Step 2: collect atoms
atoms = [i for i in mol[0].get_atoms()]

# Step 3: full Delaunay tessellation
tessellations, graph = AlphaShape(atoms, float('Inf'))

# Step 4: inspect circumsphere of first simplex
centre, radius = Circumsphere(tessellations[0])

# Step 5: alpha-filtered shape
tessellations_3, graph_3 = AlphaShape(atoms, 3)
```

Sources: [docs/source/tutorials/alpha_shape.rst:1-55]()

---

## Testing

The geometry module tests live at [packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py:1-30]() and use structure `4hla.cif` as test data.

| Test method | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `test_Circumsphere` | All three center coordinates and the radius are Python `float` instances |
| `test_AlphaShape` | Elements of the returned tessellation list are `packman.molecule.Atom` instances |

Sources: [packman/tests/geometry/test_geometry.py:9-28]()

---

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Used for |
|---|---|
| `scipy.spatial.Delaunay` | Full Delaunay tessellation of atom coordinates |
| `networkx.Graph` | Representing the atom connectivity graph output |
| `numpy.linalg.det` | Determinant computation inside `Circumsphere` |
| `packman.molecule.Atom` | Input type; `.get_location()` extracts coordinates |

Sources: [packman/geometry/geometry.py:21-29]()

This page documents the PACKMAN command-line interface (CLI): its entry point, all subcommands, their arguments, defaults, and example invocations. The CLI exposes the same four analysis applications as the Python API and GUI. For the Python API usage of each application, see [Analysis Applications](#4). For the GUI, see [Graphical User Interface](#8).

---

## Entry Point

The CLI is launched via Python's `-m` flag:

```
python -m packman <subcommand> [arguments]
```

The dispatcher `main()` in [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:141-148]() checks `sys.argv[1]`. If it equals `"gui"`, it calls `load_gui()`. Otherwise, it calls `load_cli()`, which invokes `IO()` to parse arguments and then dispatches to the appropriate `_cli` function.

**Launch GUI instead:**
```
python -m packman gui
```

---

## CLI Dispatch Architecture

**Diagram: CLI call flow from entry point to application**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    user["\"python -m packman <subcommand>\""]
    main["\"main() in PACKMAN.py\""]
    gui["\"load_gui()\""]
    cli["\"load_cli()\""]
    io["\"IO() — argparse subparsers\""]
    load["\"molecule.load_structure()\""]
    hinge_cli["\"hinge_cli(args, mol)\""]
    hdanm_cli["\"hdanm_cli(args, mol)\""]
    entropy_cli["\"entropy_cli(args, mol)\""]
    dci_cli["\"dci_cli(args, mol)\""]

    user --> main
    main -- "sys.argv[1] == 'gui'" --> gui
    main -- "otherwise" --> cli
    cli --> io
    io --> load
    load --> hinge_cli
    load --> hdanm_cli
    load --> entropy_cli
    load --> dci_cli
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:95-131](), [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:141-148]()

---

**Diagram: Subcommand to implementation mapping**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "packman/bin/PACKMAN.py"
        IO["\"IO() — defines subparsers\""]
    end
    subgraph "packman/apps/"
        hinge_cli["\"hinge_cli() in predict_hinge.py\""]
        hdanm_cli["\"hdanm_cli() in hdanm.py\""]
        entropy_cli["\"entropy_cli() in calculate_entropy.py\""]
        dci_cli["\"dci_cli() in dci.py\""]
    end

    IO -- "command == 'hinge'" --> hinge_cli
    IO -- "command == 'hdanm'" --> hdanm_cli
    IO -- "command == 'entropy'" --> entropy_cli
    IO -- "command == 'dci'" --> dci_cli
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:27-87](), [packman/apps/__init__.py:16-19]()

---

## Global Options

These options apply at the top-level parser and are primarily used by the hosted web servers:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--outputfile` | writable file | `sys.stdout` | Path to write analysis output |
| `--logfile` | writable file | `sys.stderr` | Path to write log messages |

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:82-84]()

---

## Subcommand: `hinge`

Runs hinge prediction using the alpha-shape algorithm. Implemented by `hinge_cli()` in [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:326-366]().

**Synopsis:**
```
python -m packman hinge [--pdbid PDB_ID] [--e_clusters N] [--minhnglen N]
                        [--chain CHAIN] [--generateobj FILE]
                        AlphaValue FILENAME
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AlphaValue` | float (positional) | Yes | — | Alpha parameter for the alpha-shape. Recommended: `2.8` (closed), `4.5` (open). |
| `FILENAME` | string (positional) | Yes | — | Path to the input PDB/CIF file. |
| `-pdbid` / `--pdbid` | string | No | `None` | PDB ID to download; file is saved to `FILENAME`. |
| `--e_clusters` | int | No | `4` | Number of eccentricity clusters for K-means. |
| `--minhnglen` | int | No | `5` | Minimum residue length for a predicted hinge to be reported. |
| `--chain` | string | No | `None` | Single chain ID to analyze; all chains analyzed if omitted. |
| `--generateobj` | writable binary file | No | `None` | Path to save an `.obj` file of the alpha shape. Only used when `--chain` is also provided. |

### Behavior

- If `--chain` is given, only that chain's backbone atoms are used.
- If `--chain` is omitted, all chains in `mol[0]` are iterated.
- The `--generateobj` flag is silently ignored without `--chain`.
- Output (hinge residues, statistics, p-values, PyMOL commands) is written to `--outputfile` (default: stdout).

### Examples

```bash
# Download 1prw and predict hinges on all chains, alpha=2.8
python -m packman hinge --pdbid 1prw 2.8 1prw.pdb

# Use a local file, single chain
python -m packman hinge 2.8 1prw.pdb --chain A

# Export alpha-shape mesh
python -m packman hinge 2.8 1prw.pdb --chain A --generateobj shape.obj
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:40-48](), [packman/apps/predict_hinge.py:326-366](), [docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict_cli.rst:47-79]()

---

## Subcommand: `hdanm`

Runs the Hinge-Domain ANM (hdANM) to generate mode-based motion movies. Implemented by `hdanm_cli()` imported from `packman/apps/hdanm.py`.

**Synopsis:**
```
python -m packman hdanm [--pdbid PDB_ID] [--chain CHAIN] [--dr DR]
                        [--power POWER] [--mass MASS] [--scale N]
                        [--frames N] [--modes N] [--ca_to_aa] [--make_tar]
                        FILENAME HNG
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FILENAME` | string (positional) | Yes | — | Path to the input PDB/CIF file. |
| `HNG` | string (positional) | Yes | — | Path to the `.hng` hinge definition file. |
| `-pdbid` / `--pdbid` | string | No | `None` | PDB ID to download; file saved to `FILENAME`. |
| `--chain` | string | No | `None` | Chain ID to analyze. |
| `--dr` | float | No | `15` | Distance cutoff (Å) for the ANM contact map. |
| `--power` | float | No | `0` | Exponent for distance weighting in the non-parametric ANM. |
| `--mass` | string | No | `'residue'` | Mass assignment: `unit`, `residue`, or `atom`. |
| `--scale` | int | No | `2` | Amplitude scale for generated movie frames. |
| `--frames` | int | No | `10` | Number of frames per mode movie. |
| `--modes` | int | No | `10` | Number of modes to compute and output. |
| `--ca_to_aa` | bool flag | No | `False` | Project Cα motions onto all atoms in the structure. |
| `--make_tar` | flag | No | off | Bundle all output files into a `.tar.gz` archive. |

### HNG File Format

The `.hng` file is tab-separated and defines which residue ranges are rigid domains (`D`) and which are hinges (`H`):

```
1exr.pdb_A	D1	1:70
1exr.pdb_A	H1	71:90
1exr.pdb_A	D2	91:148
```

Columns: `Filename_ChainID`, `Domain/HingeID`, `StartResidue:EndResidue`. The `.hng` file can be produced by the `hinge` subcommand or by the `ScanAlpha.py` batch utility.

### Examples

```bash
# Basic hdANM with local files
python -m packman hdanm 1exr.pdb 1exr.hng --chain A

# Download structure, custom cutoff, 20 frames
python -m packman hdanm --pdbid 1exr 1exr.pdb 1exr.hng --dr 12 --frames 20

# Package outputs
python -m packman hdanm 1exr.pdb 1exr.hng --make_tar
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:50-62](), [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM_cli.rst:24-46](), [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst:48-54]()

---

## Subcommand: `entropy`

Computes per-residue packing entropy using Voronoi tessellation. Implemented by `entropy_cli()` imported from `packman/apps/calculate_entropy.py`.

**Synopsis:**
```
python -m packman entropy [--type entropy_type] [--pdbid PDB_ID]
                          [--chains CHAINS] [--probe_size FLOAT]
                          [--onspherepoints INT]
                          FILENAME
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FILENAME` | string (positional) | Yes | — | Path to the input PDB/CIF file. |
| `-type` / `--type` | string | No | `None` | Entropy variant. Currently supported: `PackingEntropy`. |
| `-pdbid` / `--pdbid` | string | No | `None` | PDB ID to download; file saved to `FILENAME`. |
| `--chains` | string | No | `None` | Comma-separated chain IDs (e.g., `A,B`). `None` includes all chains. |
| `--probe_size` | float | No | `1.4` | Solvent probe radius in Å (water ≈ 1.4 Å). |
| `--onspherepoints` | int | No | `30` | Number of surface probe points per atom. |

### Chain Selection Note

`--chains` controls which chains are *included in the entropy calculation*, not just which chains appear in the output. To include chain C in the geometry but exclude it from reported entropy, omit `--chains` and filter the output by chain column.

### Examples

```bash
# Entropy for all chains
python -m packman entropy 1prw.pdb --type PackingEntropy

# Entropy restricted to chains A and B
python -m packman entropy 1prw.pdb --type PackingEntropy --chains A,B

# Download and run
python -m packman entropy --pdbid 1prw 1prw.pdb --type PackingEntropy
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:65-71](), [docs/source/tutorials/entropy_cli.rst:22-57]()

---

## Subcommand: `dci`

Runs Dynamic Community Identification (DCI) using GNM-based cross-correlations and hierarchical clustering. Implemented by `dci_cli()` imported from `packman/apps/dci.py`.

**Synopsis:**
```
python -m packman dci [--pdbid PDB_ID] [--chain CHAIN]
                      [--cutoff FLOAT] [--n_com INT]
                      FILENAME
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FILENAME` | string (positional) | Yes | — | Path to the input PDB/CIF file. |
| `-pdbid` / `--pdbid` | string | No | `None` | PDB ID to download; file saved to `FILENAME`. |
| `-chain` / `--chain` | string | No | `None` | Chain ID. `None` analyzes all chains. |
| `-cutoff` / `--cutoff` | float | No | `7.0` | Distance cutoff (Å) for GNM contact map construction. |
| `-n_com` / `--n_com` | int | No | `None` | Number of communities. `None` uses the Calinski-Harabasz optimal score. |

### Examples

```bash
# DCI on chain A with default cutoff
python -m packman dci 1prw.pdb --chain A

# DCI on all chains, fixed number of communities
python -m packman dci 1prw.pdb --n_com 5

# Download and run
python -m packman dci --pdbid 1prw 1prw.pdb --chain A
```

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:74-79](), [docs/source/tutorials/dci_cli.rst:22-47]()

---

## Subcommand Summary

| Subcommand | Positional Args | Key Optional Args | Implementation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hinge` | `AlphaValue`, `FILENAME` | `--chain`, `--e_clusters`, `--minhnglen`, `--generateobj` | `hinge_cli()` in `predict_hinge.py` |
| `hdanm` | `FILENAME`, `HNG` | `--chain`, `--dr`, `--mass`, `--modes`, `--frames`, `--make_tar` | `hdanm_cli()` in `hdanm.py` |
| `entropy` | `FILENAME` | `--type`, `--chains`, `--probe_size`, `--onspherepoints` | `entropy_cli()` in `calculate_entropy.py` |
| `dci` | `FILENAME` | `--chain`, `--cutoff`, `--n_com` | `dci_cli()` in `dci.py` |

All four subcommands share the `-pdbid`/`--pdbid` option for on-demand structure download.

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:27-87](), [packman/apps/__init__.py:16-19]()

---

## Structure Loading

`load_cli()` in [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:95-131]() loads the molecular structure before dispatching to any subcommand:

1. If `--pdbid` is given, `molecule.download_structure()` is called first, saving to `FILENAME`.
2. The file extension is extracted from `FILENAME` and passed as `ftype` to `molecule.load_structure()`.
3. If the extension cannot be determined, `load_structure()` is called without `ftype` and PACKMAN attempts auto-detection.

See [Loading and Downloading Structures](#3.1) for details on `load_structure()` and `download_structure()`.

Sources: [packman/bin/PACKMAN.py:112-120]()

---

## ScanAlpha Batch Utility

For scanning a range of alpha values to find consensus hinges, a standalone script is provided at [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py](). It is not part of the installed CLI but can be copied to the working directory and run directly.

```bash
python3 ScanAlpha.py myprotein.pdb --chain A --begin 0 --end 10 --step_size 0.5
```

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `filename` | required | Input PDB/CIF file |
| `--chain` | `None` | Chain ID (all chains if omitted) |
| `--begin` | `0` | Starting alpha value |
| `--end` | `10` | Ending alpha value |
| `--step_size` | `0.5` | Increment between alpha values |
| `--outfilename` | `output.hng` | Name for the output `.hng` file |

The script iterates `predict_hinge()` over all alpha values, collects overlapping significant hinges (p-value ≤ 0.05), and writes a merged `.hng` file suitable for use with the `hdanm` subcommand.

Sources: [additional codes/ScanAlpha.py:1-144]()

---

# Graphical User Interface (GUI)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/source/tutorials/gui.rst](docs/source/tutorials/gui.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst](docs/source/tutorials/hdANM.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/hdANM_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/hdANM_cli.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict_cli.rst](docs/source/tutorials/hinge_predict_cli.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/installation.rst](docs/source/tutorials/installation.rst)
- [docs/source/tutorials/main.rst](docs/source/tutorials/main.rst)
- [packman/__init__.py](packman/__init__.py)
- [packman/bin/GUI.py](packman/bin/GUI.py)
- [setup.py](setup.py)

</details>



This page documents the PACKMAN GUI: how to launch it, the structure of its panels, the input fields each panel exposes, and how results are displayed and saved. The GUI covers three analytical workflows — hinge prediction, hdANM, and Voronoi packing entropy — all within a single `tkinter` window.

For the equivalent CLI commands, see [Command-Line Interface](#7). For the Python API behind each panel, see [Analysis Applications](#4) and [Network Models](#5).

---

## Launching the GUI

```bash
python -m packman gui
# OR
python3 -m packman gui
```

The entry point is the `load_gui()` function in [packman/bin/GUI.py:112-114](), which instantiates the `Skeleton` class and starts the `tkinter` main loop.

> **Prerequisites:**
> - `tkinter` must be available. On some Linux systems it is not installed by default: `sudo apt-get install python3-tk`.
> - Output files are written to the **current working directory** at the time the GUI is launched.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:1-114](), [docs/source/tutorials/gui.rst:1-15]()

---

## Window Architecture

The `Skeleton` class is the top-level `tk.Tk` window. It owns all panel frames and a persistent top navigation bar (`top_menu`). Only one content panel is visible at a time; switching is handled by `Skeleton.show_frame()`.

**Application window layout (code entities)**

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Skeleton(tk.Tk)"] --> B["top_menu(tk.Frame)"]
    A --> C["HomePage(tk.Frame)"]
    A --> D["HingePrediction(tk.Frame)"]
    A --> E["hdANM_GUI(tk.Frame)"]
    A --> F["Voronoi_Packing_Entropy_GUI(tk.Frame)"]
    B -->|"show_frame('HomePage')"| C
    B -->|"show_frame('HingePrediction')"| D
    B -->|"show_frame('hdANM_GUI')"| E
    B -->|"show_frame('Voronoi_Packing_Entropy_GUI')"| F
```

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:53-114]()

**Class-to-panel mapping**

| Class | Navigation Label | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `HomePage` | Home | Welcome text and external links |
| `HingePrediction` | Hinge Prediction | Run `predict_hinge()`, export `.hng` |
| `hdANM_GUI` | hdANM | Run `hdANM`, save matrices/movies |
| `Voronoi_Packing_Entropy_GUI` | Packing Entropy (Voronoi) | Run `PackingEntropy`, save TSV output |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:65-70](), [packman/bin/GUI.py:97-114]()

---

## Home Panel (`HomePage`)

Displays a static description of PACKMAN and a read-only text block containing links to:

1. ReadTheDocs tutorials
2. GitHub repository
3. Online Hinge Prediction server
4. Online hdANM server
5. Online Voronoi Entropy server

No interactive inputs or computations occur on this panel.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:122-145]()

---

## Hinge Prediction Panel (`HingePrediction`)

Calls `predict_hinge()` from `packman.apps` on backbone atoms of the loaded structure.

### Input Fields

| Widget | Label | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Box1` | Filename / PDB ID | _(empty)_ | `str` — local path or 4-char PDB ID |
| `Box2` | Chain ID | _(empty)_ | `str` — leave blank to run all chains |
| `Box3` | Alpha Value | `2.8` | `float` |
| `Box4` | Number of Eccentricity Clusters | `4` | `int` |
| `Box5` | Minimum Hinge Length | `5` | `int` |
| `Browse1` | Browse button | — | Opens file dialog (`.cif`, `.pdb`) |
| `Button1` | Run | — | Triggers `run_PACKMAN()` |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:153-201]()

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User clicks Run"] --> B["molecule.load_structure(Box1)"]
    B -->|"FileNotFound"| C["molecule.download_structure(Box1)"]
    C --> B
    B --> D{"Box2 (Chain ID) provided?"}
    D -->|"Yes"| E["mol[0][chain].get_backbone()"]
    D -->|"No"| F["Iterate mol[0].get_chains()"]
    E --> G["predict_hinge(backbone, Alpha, nclusters, MinimumHingeLength)"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Open Results Popup (tk.Toplevel)"]
```

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:215-262]()

### Results Popup

A scrollable `tk.Toplevel` window (`pop_up1`) displays a table with one row per detected hinge:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Hinge ID | Sequential integer |
| PDB ID / Filename | `Box1` value |
| Chain ID | Chain the hinge belongs to |
| Residue IDs | `start:end` range |
| p-value | `hinge.get_pvalue()` |
| Select | `tk.Checkbutton` (BooleanVar) |
| Details | Opens a secondary popup via `show_details(hinge.get_stats())` |

After reviewing results, the user can select hinges and save a `.hng` file via the **Save HNG file** button, which calls the nested `write_hng_file()` function. The output filename defaults to `<Box1 value>.hng`.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:264-387]()

---

## hdANM Panel (`hdANM_GUI`)

Calls the `hdANM` class from `packman.anm`.

### Input Fields

| Widget | Label | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Box1` | Filename / PDB ID | _(empty)_ | `str` |
| `Box2` | Chain ID | _(empty)_ | `str` — blank = all chains |
| `Box3` | Cutoff Value | `15` | `float` (Å) |
| `Box4` | Power of Distance | `0` | `int` |
| `Box5` | Input (.hng) Filename | `output.hng` | `str` |
| `dropdown1` | Mass of the residue | `Molecular Weight` | One of: `Molecular Weight`, `Unit`, `Atomics Mass` |
| `Browse1` | Browse (structure) | — | Opens file dialog (`.cif`, `.pdb`) |
| `Browse2` | Browse (.hng) | — | Opens file dialog (`.hng`) |
| `Button1` | Run | — | Triggers `run_hdANM()` |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:395-458]()

### Mass Type Mapping

The dropdown selection maps to `hdANM.calculate_hessian(mass_type=...)`:

| Dropdown Value | `mass_type` Argument |
|---|---|
| `Molecular Weight` | `'residue'` |
| `Unit` | `'unit'` |
| `Atomics Mass` | `'atom'` |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:525-530]()

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User clicks Run"] --> B["molecule.load_structure(Box1)"]
    B -->|"FileNotFound"| C["molecule.download_structure(Box1)"]
    C --> B
    B --> D{"Box2 (Chain ID) provided?"}
    D -->|"Yes"| E["mol[0][chain].get_calpha()"]
    D -->|"No"| F["Iterate mol[0].get_chains()"]
    E --> G["hdANM(calpha, dr, power, hng_file)"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Model.calculate_hessian(mass_type)"]
    H --> I["Model.calculate_decomposition()"]
    I --> J["Open Results Popup (tk.Toplevel)"]
```

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:478-602]()

### Results Popup

The results popup (`pop_up1` titled `hdANM Results`) has two sections:

**Section 1 — Save Output Matrices**

| Dropdown Choice | Action |
|---|---|
| `hdANM Eigen Vectors` | Saves `Model.get_eigenvectors()` to `hdANM Eigen Vectors.csv` |
| `hdANM Eigen Values` | Saves `Model.get_eigenvalues()` to `hdANM Eigen Values.csv` |

**Section 2 — Generate Movies**

| Widget | Label | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_projection_choise` | Projection Method | `Curvilinear` | `Curvilinear` or `Linear` |
| `n_mode` | Mode Number | `6` | `int` (non-rigid modes start at index 6) |
| `n_frames` | Number of Frames | `10` | `int` |
| `n_scale` | Movie Scale | `10` | `float` |
| `ca_to_aa` | Project C-Alpha to all atoms | unchecked | `bool` |

Clicking **Save Movie** calls `Model.calculate_movie(n_mode, n=n_frames, scale=n_scale, extrapolation=projection, ca_to_aa=...)`. Output is written as `<n_mode>.pdb` or `<n_mode>.cif` in the working directory.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:535-601]()

---

## Voronoi Packing Entropy Panel (`Voronoi_Packing_Entropy_GUI`)

Calls the `PackingEntropy` class from `packman.entropy`.

### Input Fields

| Widget | Label | Default | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Box1` | Filename / PDB ID | _(empty)_ | `str` |
| `Box2` | Chain IDs (comma-separated) | _(empty)_ | `str` — blank = all chains |
| `Box3` | Probe size | `1.4` | `float` (Å) |
| `Box4` | On Sphere Points | `30` | `int` |
| `Box5` | Output Filename | `voronoi_packing_entropy_output.txt` | `str` |
| `Browse1` | Browse | — | Opens file dialog (`.cif`, `.pdb`) |
| `Button1` | Run | — | Triggers `run_Entropy()` |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:610-658]()

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User clicks Run"] --> B["molecule.load_structure(Box1)"]
    B -->|"FileNotFound"| C["molecule.download_structure(Box1)"]
    C --> B
    B --> D["Parse Box2 as chain list"]
    D --> E["PackingEntropy(atoms, chains, probe_size, onspherepoints)"]
    E --> F["Iterate mol frames and residues"]
    F --> G["Write TSV to Box5 output file"]
    G --> H["showinfo notification"]
```

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:673-734]()

### Output File Format

The output is a tab-separated file written to the path specified in `Box5`. Each row is one residue per frame:

```
Frame   Chain   ResidueID   ResidueName   PackingEntropy
```

After all per-residue rows, two summary lines are appended per frame:
- `Total (Frame N)` — `result.get_total_entropy()`
- `Total Normalized Entropy (3N-6) (Frame N)` — total divided by `3N - 6`

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:712-729]()

---

## Chain ID Behavior (All Panels)

All three analysis panels share the same convention for the Chain ID field:

- **Provided**: Runs the analysis only on the specified chain.
- **Left blank**: Runs the analysis on all chains in the structure.
- For the entropy panel, the chain list is comma-separated and controls which chains are included in the `PackingEntropy` calculation (affects neighbor context, not just output filtering). See [Packing Entropy](#4.3) for the distinction.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:246-262](), [packman/bin/GUI.py:505-520](), [packman/bin/GUI.py:704-710]()

---

## File Auto-Download

All panels that accept a structure file attempt `molecule.download_structure()` if `molecule.load_structure()` raises an exception. The logic tries to infer the file type from the extension:

```
molecule.download_structure(Box1.split('.')[0], ftype=Box1.split('.')[1])
```

If that fails, it falls back to `molecule.download_structure(Box1)`. A notification dialog is shown before the download attempt, and an error dialog is shown if the download fails.

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:219-236](), [packman/bin/GUI.py:479-496](), [packman/bin/GUI.py:677-694]()

---

## Platform Notes

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Window icon | Loaded from `packman/bin/logo.ico`; silently skipped on non-Windows platforms |
| `tkinter` availability | Built into Python on Windows and macOS; may require `python3-tk` on Linux |
| Window size | Fixed at 800×600 px (`Skeleton.__init__`) |
| Output location | All files written to the **current working directory** |

Sources: [packman/bin/GUI.py:72-88](), [setup.py:38-39](), [docs/source/tutorials/gui.rst:12-15]()
